Step 3: Positive points go on the right of 0: mark 3 and 6, and also mark 0.

Final answer: From left to right the points stand as −13, −11, −8, 0, 3, 6.

Q9(ii). Draw a number line and represent the points 3, 8, 5, −11, −5 and −7 on it.

Step 1: Draw a number line from −11 to 8 with equal steps and mark 0.

Step 2: Negative points go on the left of 0: mark −11, −7 and −5.

Step 3: Positive points go on the right of 0: mark 3, 5 and 8.

Final answer: From left to right the points stand as −11, −7, −5, 3, 5, 8.

Q10. Write the opposite for the following integers: (i) 14 (ii) −24 (iii) 65 (iv) −39 (v) 0 (vi) −420.

Step 1: The opposite of an integer is the integer at the same distance from zero on the other side; only the sign changes.

Step 2: (i) Opposite of 14 is −14. (ii) Opposite of −24 is +24. (iii) Opposite of 65 is −65.

Step 3: (iv) Opposite of −39 is +39. (v) Opposite of 0 is 0. (vi) Opposite of −420 is +420.

Final answer: (i) −14 (ii) +24 (iii) −65 (iv) +39 (v) 0 (vi) +420.

Q11. Identify the integers in the following numbers: +12, −21.4, −17, 1 2/5, 3 9/11, +11.25, 18.4, +26, −57, 0.

Step 1: Integers have no decimal part and no fractional part.

Step 2: +12, −17, +26, −57 and 0 satisfy this, so they are integers.

Step 3: −21.4, +11.25 and 18.4 have decimal parts, and 1 2/5 and 3 9/11 are fractions, so they are not integers.

Final answer: Integers: +12, −17, +26, −57, 0.

Q12. Hadi has Rs. 12 in his pocket, but Neelam gives him Rs. 4 and Hamza gives him Rs. 3. How much money has Hadi in all? Show all this information on a number line.

Step 1: Money Hadi already has = Rs. 12. On the number line, start at 12.

Step 2: Neelam gives Rs. 4, so move 4 steps to the right: 12 + 4 = 16.

Step 3: Hamza gives Rs. 3, so move 3 more steps to the right: 16 + 3 = 19.

Final answer: Hadi has Rs. 19 in all.

Q13. Describe and show your position on a number line, if you begin at 8, move right 8 steps and then move left 8 steps.

Step 1: Begin at 8 on the number line.

Step 2: Move right 8 steps: 8 + 8 = 16, reaching 16.

Step 3: Move left 8 steps: 16 − 8 = 8, reaching 8.

Final answer: You come back to 8, your starting position.

Q14. When Saba woke up, her temperature was 101°F. Two hours later it was 4°F lower. What was her temperature then?

Step 1: Starting temperature = 101°F.

Step 2: Lower by 4°F means subtract 4: 101 − 4 = 97.

Final answer: Her temperature was 97°F.

mcqs.q: On the number line, where do the positive integers +1, +2, +3, ... lie?
options: On the left side of zero
On the right side of zero
mcqs.why: The notes place zero in the middle, with positive integers +1, +2, +3, ... on the right side of zero at equal distances.

mcqs.q: On the number line, where do the negative integers -1, -2, -3, ... lie?
options: On the right side of zero
On the left side of zero
mcqs.why: The notes place the negative integers -1, -2, -3, ... on the left side of zero, all at equal distances from each other.

mcqs.q: How is -4 read?
mcqs.why: The notes state that -4 is read as 'Negative 4' and written -4, while +4 is read as 'Positive 4'.

mcqs.q: Two integers are opposite (additive inverse) if they are:
options: At the same distance from zero but on opposite sides of zero
Next to each other on the same side
mcqs.why: Opposite integers are at the same distance from zero on the number line but on opposite sides of zero, for example +4 and -4.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite integer of -24?
mcqs.why: The opposite changes only the sign while keeping the same distance from zero, so the opposite of -24 is +24, as in Exercise 2.1 Q10.

mcqs.q: To represent -13 on a number line, you should count:
mcqs.why: Book Example 2 counts 13 steps towards the left of 0 for -13, because negative integers lie on the left side of zero.

mcqs.q: What are the natural numbers between 4 and 11?
mcqs.why: Working: 'between 4 and 11' means greater than 4 and less than 11, so we exclude 4 and 11 and list 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10.

mcqs.q: Hadi has Rs. 12, Neelam gives him Rs. 4 and Hamza gives him Rs. 3. How much has Hadi in all?
mcqs.why: Working: start with 12, add Neelam's 4 to get 12 + 4 = 16, then add Hamza's 3 to get 16 + 3 = 19, so Hadi has Rs. 19.

mcqs.q: You begin at 8, move right 8 steps and then move left 8 steps. Where do you finish?
mcqs.why: Working: moving right gives 8 + 8 = 16, then moving left gives 16 - 8 = 8, so you come back to your starting position 8.

mcqs.q: Saba's temperature was 101 F and two hours later it was 4 F lower. What was her temperature then?
mcqs.why: Working: lower by 4 F means subtract 4, so 101 - 4 = 97, therefore her temperature was 97 F after two hours.

lessons.title: 2.3 ABSOLUTE OR NUMERICAL VALUE OF AN INTEGER
lessons.notes_html:
Absolute or Numerical Value of an Integer

The concept of absolute value has many uses. We know about the number line. Every integer on the number line represents a distance from zero.

For example, Fatima is moving 10 steps to east and Shahid is moving 10 steps to west from the origin on the number line. Fatima is standing at point −10 and Shahid is standing at point +10, but both cover the same distance from the origin.

So, we can say that "Absolute value or numerical value of a number is its distance from zero on the number line and it is always positive or zero."

It is always denoted by the symbol | |. In the above example, distance 10 left from zero can be written as |−10| and read as: the absolute value of −10 is 10.

mcqs.q: The absolute or numerical value of a number is defined as its:
options: Distance from zero on the number line
Position to the left of zero
mcqs.why: The notes define absolute value as a number's distance from zero on the number line, regardless of which side of zero it lies on.

mcqs.q: The absolute value of an integer is always:
mcqs.why: Because absolute value is a distance from zero, the notes state it is always positive or zero; a distance can never be negative.

mcqs.q: Which symbol is used to denote absolute value?
mcqs.why: Absolute value is always denoted by the symbol | |, for example the distance 10 left from zero is written as |-10|.

mcqs.q: What is the value of |-10|?
mcqs.why: Working: |-10| is the distance of -10 from zero on the number line, which is 10 steps, so |-10| = 10.

mcqs.q: In the example, Fatima stands at point -10 and Shahid stands at point +10. What distance does each cover from the origin?
mcqs.why: Working: distance of -10 from 0 is |-10| = 10 and distance of +10 from 0 is |+10| = 10, so both cover the same distance of 10 steps.

mcqs.q: How is |-10| read in words?
mcqs.why: The notes read |-10| as: the absolute value of -10 is 10, because -10 lies 10 steps away from zero on the number line.

mcqs.q: Which two integers in the example have the same absolute value?
mcqs.why: Working: |-10| = 10 and |+10| = 10, so -10 and +10 have the same absolute value even though they are on opposite sides of zero.

mcqs.q: If a point is at -10 on the number line, its distance from zero is:
mcqs.why: Working: distance is measured as an absolute value, so the distance of -10 from zero is |-10| = 10, never a negative number.

mcqs.q: Fatima moves 10 steps to one side and Shahid moves 10 steps to the opposite side. Their distances from the origin are:
mcqs.why: Both stand 10 steps away from the origin, one at -10 and one at +10, so the notes conclude both cover the same distance from the origin.

mcqs.q: Every integer on the number line represents what in relation to zero, for absolute value?
mcqs.why: The lesson begins by stating that every integer on the number line represents a distance from zero, and that distance is its absolute value.

lessons.title: 2.3.1 Arrangement of absolute values of the given integers in ascending or descending order
lessons.notes_html:
Arrangement of absolute values in ascending or descending order

Look at the following examples to understand the concept of ascending and descending order of absolute values. Ascending order means arranging from smallest to greatest, and descending order means arranging from greatest to smallest. First find the absolute value of every integer, then arrange those values.

Book Example 3 — Ascending order of absolute values

Arrange the absolute values of the following numbers in ascending order: 7, −14, 0, 15, −12, −2, 11.

Step 1: Find each absolute value: |7| = 7, |−14| = 14, |0| = 0, |15| = 15, |−12| = 12, |−2| = 2 and |11| = 11.

Step 2: Arrange these values from smallest to greatest: 0, 2, 7, 11, 12, 14, 15.

Final answer: The required arrangement in ascending order of absolute values is 0, 2, 7, 11, 12, 14, 15.

Book Example 4 — Descending order of absolute values

Arrange the absolute values of the following numbers in descending order: −6, 3, −13, 5, 0, −2, 12, −18.

Step 1: Find each absolute value: |−6| = 6, |3| = 3, |−13| = 13, |5| = 5, |0| = 0, |−2| = 2, |12| = 12 and |−18| = 18.

Step 2: Arrange these values from greatest to smallest: 18, 13, 12, 6, 5, 3, 2, 0.

Final answer: The required arrangement in descending order of absolute values is 18, 13, 12, 6, 5, 3, 2, 0.

Book Example 5 — Ascending order using the number line

Use a number line to arrange the following numbers in ascending order: −2, −13, −18, |−5|, 3, −19, |−1|, |−12|.

Step 1: First find the absolute values: |−5| = 5, |−1| = 1 and |−12| = 12.

Step 2: The numbers become −2, −13, −18, 5, 3, −19, 1, 12. Place them on the number line; the leftmost number is the smallest.

Step 3: Reading the number line from left to right gives the ascending order.

Final answer: Ascending order: −19, −18, −13, −2, 1, 3, 5, 12.

Book Example 6 — Descending order using the number line

Use a number line to arrange the following numbers in descending order: |−1|, −11, 4, |−9|, −7, −18, |−7|, 16.

Step 1: First find the absolute values: |−1| = 1, |−9| = 9 and |−7| = 7.

Step 2: The numbers become 1, −11, 4, 9, −7, −18, 7, 16. Place them on the number line; the rightmost number is the greatest.

Step 3: Reading the number line from right to left gives the descending order.

Final answer: Descending order: 16, 9, 7, 4, 1, −7, −11, −18.

Worked examples — Exercise 2.2

Q1(i). Arrange the following integers in ascending order: −7, 0, −4, 4, 3, −2, 1.

Step 1: On the number line, negative integers are on the left of 0 and positive integers on the right.

Step 2: The negatives from smallest to greatest are −7, −4, −2; then comes 0; then the positives 1, 3, 4.

Final answer: −7, −4, −2, 0, 1, 3, 4.

Q1(ii). Arrange the following integers in ascending order: −1, −6, 7, −3, 0, 6, 17.

Step 1: The negatives from smallest to greatest are −6, −3, −1; then comes 0; then the positives 6, 7, 17.

Final answer: −6, −3, −1, 0, 6, 7, 17.

Q2(i). Arrange the following integers in descending order: −4, −2, 7, 16, 0, −1.

Step 1: Descending order is greatest to smallest: positives first, then 0, then negatives.

Step 2: Positives: 16, 7; then 0; then negatives: −1, −2, −4.

Final answer: 16, 7, 0, −1, −2, −4.

Q2(ii). Arrange the following integers in descending order: 13, 24, −10, 0, 8, 5.

Step 1: Positives from greatest to smallest: 24, 13, 8, 5; then 0; then the negative −10.

Final answer: 24, 13, 8, 5, 0, −10.

Q3. Write the absolute or numerical value of the following integers: (i) −45 (ii) 116 (iii) −209 (iv) 0 (v) −2813 (vi) −501.

Step 1: The absolute value is the distance from zero, so it is always positive or zero; we simply drop the negative sign.

Step 2: (i) |−45| = 45. (ii) |116| = 116. (iii) |−209| = 209.

Step 3: (iv) |0| = 0. (v) |−2813| = 2813. (vi) |−501| = 501.

Final answer: (i) 45 (ii) 116 (iii) 209 (iv) 0 (v) 2813 (vi) 501.

Q4(i). Arrange the absolute values of the following integers in ascending order: −13, 0, −4, 12, 16, −9, 17.

Step 1: Find the absolute values: |−13| = 13, |0| = 0, |−4| = 4, |12| = 12, |16| = 16, |−9| = 9, |17| = 17.

Step 2: Arrange from smallest to greatest: 0, 4, 9, 12, 13, 16, 17.

Final answer: 0, 4, 9, 12, 13, 16, 17.

Q4(ii). Arrange the absolute values of the following integers in ascending order: −18, 14, −12, −84, 44, 48.

Step 1: Find the absolute values: |−18| = 18, |14| = 14, |−12| = 12, |−84| = 84, |44| = 44, |48| = 48.

Step 2: Arrange from smallest to greatest: 12, 14, 18, 44, 48, 84.

Final answer: 12, 14, 18, 44, 48, 84.

Q5(i). Arrange the absolute values of the following integers in descending order: 34, −9, 12, 17, −16, −21.

Step 1: Find the absolute values: |34| = 34, |−9| = 9, |12| = 12, |17| = 17, |−16| = 16, |−21| = 21.

Step 2: Arrange from greatest to smallest: 34, 21, 17, 16, 12, 9.

Final answer: 34, 21, 17, 16, 12, 9.

Q5(ii). Arrange the absolute values of the following integers in descending order: 109, −215, 0, −85, −141, 149, 215.

Step 1: Find the absolute values: |109| = 109, |−215| = 215, |0| = 0, |−85| = 85, |−141| = 141, |149| = 149, |215| = 215.

Step 2: Arrange from greatest to smallest: 215, 215, 149, 141, 109, 85, 0.

Final answer: 215, 215, 149, 141, 109, 85, 0.

Summary of Sub-Domain 2

  • Natural numbers are counting numbers. The set of natural numbers is denoted by the capital letter 'N', e.g. N = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, …}
  • The number zero (0) together with the natural or counting numbers gives us the list of whole numbers. The set of whole numbers is denoted by 'W', e.g. W = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, …}
  • Positive integers are numbers greater than zero (0); they lie to the right of zero (0) on the number line.
  • Negative integers are numbers less than zero (0); they lie to the left of zero (0) on the number line.
  • The set of integers is {0, ±1, ±2, ±3, …}.
  • Zero (0) is an integer which is neither positive nor negative.
  • Any number on the number line lying to the left of zero (0) is negative, and any number lying to the right of zero (0) is positive.
  • The positive distance from zero (0) to any number on the number line is called absolute value, and the absolute value of a number is always positive.

mcqs.q: Ascending order means arranging values:
mcqs.why: The notes define ascending order as arranging from smallest to greatest, and descending order as arranging from greatest to smallest.

mcqs.q: What is the first step when arranging absolute values in order?
options: Find the absolute value of every integer, then arrange those values
mcqs.why: The method in the notes is to first find the absolute value of every integer and only then arrange those values in the required order.

mcqs.q: Arrange the absolute values of 7, -14, 0, 15, -12, -2, 11 in ascending order.
Arrange the absolute values of -6, 3, -13, 5, 0, -2, 12, -18 in descending order.
mcqs.why: Working: absolute values are 6, 3, 13, 5, 0, 2, 12, 18; greatest to smallest gives 18, 13, 12, 6, 5, 3, 2, 0.

mcqs.q: Using a number line, arrange -2, -13, -18, |-5|, 3, -19, |-1|, |-12| in ascending order.
Using a number line, arrange |-1|, -11, 4, |-9|, -7, -18, |-7|, 16 in descending order.
What is the absolute or numerical value of -2813?
mcqs.why: Working: absolute value is the distance from zero, so we drop the negative sign: |-2813| = 2813, as in Exercise 2.2 Q3.

mcqs.q: Arrange the absolute values of -13, 0, -4, 12, 16, -9, 17 in ascending order.
Arrange the absolute values of 34, -9, 12, 17, -16, -21 in descending order.
mcqs.why: Working: absolute values are |34|=34, |-9|=9, |12|=12, |17|=17, |-16|=16, |-21|=21; greatest to smallest gives 34, 21, 17, 16, 12, 9.

mcqs.q: Arrange the absolute values of 109, -215, 0, -85, -141, 149, 215 in descending order.
mcqs.why: Working: absolute values are 109, 215, 0, 85, 141, 149, 215; greatest to smallest gives 215, 215, 149, 141, 109, 85, 0.

chapters.title: Unit 3: Numbers and Operations — Sub-Domain 3: Laws of Integers

lessons.title: 3.1.1 Addition of Integers
lessons.notes_html:
Students' Learning Outcomes

By the end of this sub-domain, students will be able to:

  • Add up to 2-digit like and unlike integers.
  • Verify commutative and associative laws (of addition).
  • Subtract up to 2-digit like and unlike integers.
  • Multiply up to 2-digit like and unlike integers.
  • Verify commutative, associative and distributive laws (of multiplication).
  • Divide like and unlike integers up to 2-digits.

Addition and subtraction up to 2-digits like and unlike integers

A number line can also be used to find the sum or difference between given integers. The addition of integers is same as the addition of whole numbers using a number line, but there is a slight difference: on the number line, when we add the positive integers we move towards right and when we add the negative integers we move towards left.

Remember: The integers with the same signs are called like integers. The integers with different signs are called unlike integers.

Sum of two or more like integers

To find the sum, we add the given numbers. The procedure to find the sum of two or more given negative integers is in the following examples.

Book Example 1 — Sum of −6 and −7 on the number line

Use a number line to find the sum of −6 and −7: (−6) + (−7).

Step 1: Draw a number line.

Step 2: Consider 0 as the starting point and move 6 steps towards the left, reaching at −6.

Step 3: Now move 7 more steps towards the left, reaching at −13.

Final answer: (−6) + (−7) = −13.

Book Example 2 — Sum of −4, −5 and −6 on the number line

Use a number line to find the sum of −4, −5 and −6: (−4) + (−5) + (−6).

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 4 steps towards the left, reaching at −4.

Step 2: Move 5 more steps towards the left, reaching at −9.

Step 3: Move 6 more steps towards the left, reaching at −15.

Final answer: (−4) + (−5) + (−6) = −15.

Book Example 3 — Sum of 6 and 7 on the number line

Use a number line to find the sum of 6 and 7: (+6) + (+7).

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 6 steps towards the right, reaching at +6.

Step 2: Move 7 more steps towards the right, reaching at +13.

Final answer: (+6) + (+7) = +13.

Sum of unlike integers

The procedure to find the sum of two given integers with different signs is illustrated in the following examples.

Book Example 4 — Sum of 15 and −9 on the number line

Use a number line to find the sum of 15 and −9: (+15) + (−9).

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 15 steps towards the right, reaching at +15.

Step 2: Adding −9 means moving 9 steps back towards the left: 15 − 9 = 6.

Final answer: (+15) + (−9) = +15 − 9 = +6.

Book Example 5 — Sum of −4 and 13 on the number line

Use a number line to find the sum of −4 and 13: (−4) + (+13).

Step 1: Consider "0" as the starting point and move 4 steps towards the left, reaching at −4.

Step 2: Then move 13 steps towards the right: −4 + 13 = +9.

Final answer: (−4) + (+13) = −4 + 13 = +9.

Practice-1 — Use a number line to find the sum of

(i) 5 and −7

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 5 steps towards the right, reaching at 5.

Step 2: Adding −7 means moving 7 steps towards the left: 5 − 7 = −2.

Final answer: 5 + (−7) = −2.

(ii) −11 and −5

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 11 steps towards the left, reaching at −11.

Step 2: Move 5 more steps towards the left: −11 − 5 = −16.

Final answer: (−11) + (−5) = −16.

(iii) −8 and 18

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 8 steps towards the left, reaching at −8.

Step 2: Move 18 steps towards the right: −8 + 18 = 10.

Final answer: (−8) + 18 = 10.

(iv) 6 and 10

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 6 steps towards the right, reaching at 6.

Step 2: Move 10 more steps towards the right: 6 + 10 = 16.

Final answer: 6 + 10 = 16.

mcqs.q: What are like integers?
mcqs.why: The notes define like integers as integers with the same signs, for example -6 and -7 are both negative, so they are like integers.

mcqs.q: Using a number line, what is (-6) + (-7)?
mcqs.why: Start at 0, move 6 steps left to -6, then move 7 more steps left: -6 - 7 = -13, so (-6) + (-7) = -13.
Both integers are positive, so move right on the number line: 6 + 7 = 13, therefore (+6) + (+7) = +13.
Add the negative integers step by step: -4 - 5 = -9, and then -9 - 6 = -15, so the total sum is -15.
Move 15 steps right, then adding -9 moves 9 steps back to the left: 15 - 9 = 6, so (+15) + (-9) = +6.
Start at -4 and move 13 steps to the right: -4 + 13 = 9, because 13 - 4 = 9 and the result is positive.

mcqs.q: Using a number line, what is 5 + (-7)?
mcqs.why: Start at 5 and move 7 steps to the left for -7: 5 - 7 = -2, so 5 + (-7) = -2.
Both integers are negative, so keep moving left: -11 - 5 = -16, therefore (-11) + (-5) = -16.

mcqs.q: What is (-8) + 18?
mcqs.why: Start at -8 and move 18 steps to the right: -8 + 18 = 10, because 18 - 8 = 10.

mcqs.q: On a number line, in which direction do we move when we add a negative integer?
mcqs.why: The notes state that adding positive integers moves us towards the right, while adding negative integers moves us towards the left on the number line.

lessons.title: 3.1.2 Subtraction of Integers
lessons.notes_html:
Subtraction of Integers

Since subtraction is the inverse process of addition, a number line can be used to find the difference between two integers. The word "difference" is a key word that means subtraction. The same procedure can be used to subtract integers which we have used to add integers using a number line. To find the difference, we subtract the given numbers.

Recognize subtraction as the inverse process of addition

Subtraction is the inverse process of addition because "subtracting" a positive integer (subtrahend) from another given positive integer is the same as adding a negative integer (subtrahend) with reverse direction in another given positive integer.

Subtraction of like integers — Book Example 6

Subtract: (i) 9 from 14 (ii) −15 from −9.

Step 1: (i) Write it as (+14) − (+9). "Subtracting" +9 from 14 is the same as "adding" 14 to −9.

Step 2: On the number line, from 0 move 14 units to the right, then move 9 units back to the left.

Step 3: We reach at +5, so (+14) − (+9) = +5.

Step 4: (ii) Write it as (−9) − (−15) = −9 + 15.

Step 5: Subtracting (−15) from (−9) is the same as adding (−9) to 15; on the number line this brings us to +6.

Final answer: (i) (+14) − (+9) = +5 (ii) (−9) − (−15) = +6.

Subtraction of unlike integers — Book Example 7

Subtract: (i) +5 from −12 (ii) 13 from −5.

Step 1: (i) Write it as (−12) − (+5) = −12 − 5.

Step 2: Subtracting +5 from −12 is the same as adding −12 to −5; on the number line, from −12 move 5 more units to the left.

Step 3: We reach at −17, so (−12) − (+5) = −17.

Step 4: (ii) Write it as (−5) − (+13) = −5 − 13.

Step 5: Subtracting (+13) from (−5) is the same as adding (−5) to −13; on the number line, from −5 move 13 more units to the left.

Final answer: (i) (−12) − (+5) = −17 (ii) (−5) − (+13) = −18.

Practice-2 — Use a number line to subtract the following integers

(i) 8 and 17

Step 1: Write the first integer and subtract the second from it: 8 − 17.

Step 2: On the number line, start at 8 and move 17 steps towards the left.

Final answer: 8 − 17 = −9.

(ii) −9 and −14

Step 1: Write (−9) − (−14). Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its positive: −9 + 14.

Step 2: On the number line, start at −9 and move 14 steps towards the right.

Final answer: (−9) − (−14) = +5.

(iii) −11 and 7

Step 1: Write (−11) − 7 = −11 − 7.

Step 2: On the number line, start at −11 and move 7 steps towards the left.

Final answer: (−11) − 7 = −18.

(iv) 8 and −16

Step 1: Write 8 − (−16). Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its positive: 8 + 16.

Step 2: On the number line, start at 8 and move 16 steps towards the right.

Final answer: 8 − (−16) = 24.

mcqs.q: Subtraction is the inverse process of which operation?
mcqs.why: The notes state that subtraction is the inverse process of addition, and subtracting a positive integer is the same as adding a negative integer.
Subtracting +9 from 14 is the same as moving 9 units back from 14: 14 - 9 = 5, so (+14) - (+9) = +5.
Change the subtraction of -15 into addition: (-9) - (-15) = -9 + 15 = 6, so the answer is +6.
Subtracting +5 from -12 means moving 5 more units to the left: -12 - 5 = -17, so (-12) - (+5) = -17.
From -5, subtracting +13 moves 13 more units to the left: -5 - 13 = -18, so (-5) - (+13) = -18.

mcqs.q: Using a number line, what is 8 - 17?
mcqs.why: Start at 8 and move 17 steps to the left: 8 - 17 = -(17 - 8) = -9, so 8 - 17 = -9.
Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its positive: (-9) - (-14) = -9 + 14 = 5.

mcqs.q: What is (-11) - 7?
mcqs.why: Write it as -11 - 7 and move 7 steps left from -11: -11 - 7 = -18, so the difference is -18.

mcqs.q: What is 8 - (-16)?
mcqs.why: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its positive: 8 - (-16) = 8 + 16 = 24.

mcqs.q: In the notes, the word 'difference' is a key word that means which operation?
mcqs.why: The notes state clearly that the word 'difference' is a key word that means subtraction, so we subtract the given numbers to find it.

lessons.title: 3.1.3 Subtraction of one Integer from the other by changing the sign of the Integer
lessons.notes_html:
Subtraction of one integer from the other by changing the sign of the integer

The following rule can be used to subtract an integer from another integer:

Rule: Change the sign of the integer to be subtracted and add according to the rules of addition.

Remember: While doing subtracting, always write the greater integer first.

Book Example 8 — Simplify the following

(i) (+9) − (+4)

Step 1: Both integers are positive; subtract the smaller from the greater and keep the positive sign: + (9 − 4).

Final answer: (+9) − (+4) = +5.

(ii) (+16) − (−7)

Step 1: Change the sign of the integer to be subtracted: −(−7) becomes +7.

Step 2: Add according to the rules of addition: + (16 + 7) = +23.

Final answer: (+16) − (−7) = +23.

(iii) (−40) − (−26)

Step 1: Change the sign of (−26) to +26: −40 + 26.

Step 2: These are unlike integers; subtract and keep the sign of the greater value: − (40 − 26) = −14.

Final answer: (−40) − (−26) = −14.

(iv) (−68) − (+43)

Step 1: Change the sign of (+43) to −43: −68 − 43.

Step 2: Both are now negative; add and keep the negative sign: − (68 + 43) = −111.

Final answer: (−68) − (+43) = −111.

Book Example 9 — Temperature of Lahore

In the holy month of Ramadan at noon on a Friday, the temperature of Lahore was +41°C. At the time of opening roza the temperature was decreased by 13°C. What was the temperature at the time of opening the roza?

Step 1: Temperature at noon = +41°C.

Step 2: Decrease in temperature till opening time of roza = 13°C.

Step 3: Temperature at opening time of roza = (+41°C) − (+13°C) = + (41°C − 13°C) = +28°C.

Final answer: The temperature at the opening time of roza was +28°C.

Practice-3 — Subtract the following by changing the signs

(i) (−37) − (+14)

Step 1: Change the sign of (+14) to −14: −37 − 14.

Step 2: Add the two negative integers: − (37 + 14) = −51.

Final answer: (−37) − (+14) = −51.

(ii) (−94) − (−29)

Step 1: Change the sign of (−29) to +29: −94 + 29.

Step 2: Subtract the smaller value from the greater and keep the sign of the greater value: − (94 − 29) = −65.

Final answer: (−94) − (−29) = −65.

mcqs.q: What is the rule for subtracting one integer from another by changing the sign?
options: Change the sign of the integer to be subtracted and add
Change the sign of the first integer and subtract
Divide the first integer by the second
mcqs.why: The rule in the notes is: change the sign of the integer to be subtracted and then add according to the rules of addition.
Both integers are positive, so subtract the smaller from the greater and keep the positive sign: +(9 - 4) = +5.
Change the sign of the integer to be subtracted: -(-7) becomes +7, then add: 16 + 7 = 23, so the answer is +23.
Change the sign of -26 to +26: -40 + 26 = -(40 - 26) = -14, keeping the sign of the greater value, 40.
Change the sign of +43 to -43: -68 - 43 = -(68 + 43) = -111, because both integers are now negative.

mcqs.q: The temperature of Lahore was +41°C at noon and decreased by 13°C by the opening of roza. What was the temperature then?
mcqs.why: Temperature at opening time = (+41°C) - (+13°C) = +(41 - 13)°C = +28°C, as worked out in the book example.
Change the sign of +14 to -14: -37 - 14 = -(37 + 14) = -51, because both integers are now negative.
Change the sign of -29 to +29: -94 + 29 = -(94 - 29) = -65, keeping the sign of the greater value, 94.

mcqs.q: While subtracting, the notes say we should always write which integer first?
mcqs.why: The notes remind us: while doing subtraction, always write the greater integer first, then change the sign of the other integer and add.

mcqs.q: In (+16) - (-7), after changing the sign of the integer to be subtracted, -7 becomes what?
mcqs.why: The integer to be subtracted is -7, and changing its sign gives +7, so (+16) - (-7) becomes 16 + 7 = 23.

lessons.title: 3.1.4 Addition and Subtraction of Integers without using number line
lessons.notes_html:
Addition and subtraction of integers without using the number line

We know how to find the sum and difference of integers using a number line. Now in this section we will learn about addition and subtraction of two integers without using the number line. Here we will use the simple rule of addition and subtraction. We can perform the four basic mathematical operations (+, −, ×, ÷) on integers.

Addition of two integers with like signs

To add the given integers with like signs, simply follow the method illustrated in the following example.

Book Example 10 — Find the sum of

(i) +14 and +19

Step 1: Both integers are positive; add their values: + (14 + 19) = +33.

Step 2: As the common sign is '+', so the sum is positive.

Final answer: +14 + +19 = +33.

(ii) −11 and −16

Step 1: Both integers are negative; add their values: − (11 + 16) = −27.

Step 2: As the common sign is '−', so the sum is negative.

Final answer: −11 + −16 = −27.

Practice-4 — Find the sum of

(i) 18 and 19

Step 1: Both are positive with the like sign '+': + (18 + 19) = +37.

Final answer: 18 + 19 = 37.

(ii) −29 and −57

Step 1: Both are negative with the like sign '−': − (29 + 57) = −86.

Final answer: −29 + −57 = −86.

Addition of two integers with unlike signs

Remember: While adding two integers with different signs, simply subtract the integers and put the sign with the result which is the greater valued sign. Note: The sum of any integer with zero (0) always gives the same integer in result.

Book Example 11 — Find the sum of

(i) −16 and +11

Step 1: Write (−16) + (+11) = −16 + 11.

Step 2: Subtract the values: 16 − 11 = 5. The sign of the greater value (16) is negative, so the result is negative.

Final answer: (−16) + (+11) = −5.

(ii) +70 and −22

Step 1: Write (+70) + (−22) = 70 − 22.

Step 2: 70 − 22 = 48. The sign of the greater value (70) is positive, so the result is positive.

Final answer: (+70) + (−22) = 48.

(iii) 0 and −70

Step 1: Write (0) + (−70) = 0 − 70.

Step 2: The sign of the greater value (70) is negative, so the result is negative: −70.

Final answer: (0) + (−70) = −70.

(iv) +31 and 0

Step 1: Write (+31) + (0) = +31 + 0.

Step 2: Adding zero gives the same integer, and the sign of the greater value is positive.

Final answer: (+31) + (0) = +31.

Practice-5 — Find the sum of

(i) 13 and −18

Step 1: Write 13 + (−18) = 13 − 18.

Step 2: Subtract the values: 18 − 13 = 5, and put the sign of the greater value (18), which is negative.

Final answer: 13 + (−18) = −5.

(ii) −27 and 48

Step 1: Write (−27) + 48 = 48 − 27.

Step 2: 48 − 27 = 21, and the sign of the greater value (48) is positive.

Final answer: −27 + 48 = 21.

mcqs.q: Without using a number line, what is +14 + +19?
mcqs.why: Both integers are positive with like signs, so add their values and keep the positive sign: +(14 + 19) = +33.

mcqs.q: What is -11 + -16?
mcqs.why: Both integers are negative with like signs, so add their values and keep the negative sign: -(11 + 16) = -27.

mcqs.q: What is -29 + -57?
mcqs.why: Both integers are negative, so add their values and keep the common negative sign: -(29 + 57) = -86.

mcqs.q: When adding two integers with unlike signs, what rule do the notes give?
options: Add the values and keep a positive sign
Subtract the values and use the sign of the greater value
mcqs.why: For unlike signs, the notes say to subtract the integers and put the sign of the greater valued integer with the result.
The signs are unlike: subtract the values, 16 - 11 = 5, and use the sign of the greater value 16, which is negative: -5.
The signs are unlike: 70 - 22 = 48, and the sign of the greater value 70 is positive, so the sum is 48.
The sum of any integer with zero is the same integer: 0 + (-70) = -70, and the greater value 70 also carries the negative sign.
Adding zero always gives the same integer: (+31) + 0 = 31 + 0 = +31, so the integer remains unchanged.

mcqs.q: What is 13 + (-18)?
mcqs.why: Write it as 13 - 18: subtract the values, 18 - 13 = 5, and use the sign of the greater value 18, which is negative: -5.

mcqs.q: What is -27 + 48?
mcqs.why: The signs are unlike: subtract the values, 48 - 27 = 21, and use the sign of the greater value 48, which is positive: 21.

lessons.title: 3.2 VERIFICATION OF COMMUTATIVE AND ASSOCIATIVE LAWS
lessons.notes_html:
Verification of commutative and associative laws

The following laws of addition are true for integers.

Commutative law of addition

According to this law of addition, the sum of two integers remains unchanged by changing the "order". For example, 2 + 3 = 3 + 2 ⇒ 5 = 5.

Remember: Commutative law with respect to subtraction does not hold, e.g. 8 − 3 ≠ 3 − 8.

Book Example 12 — Verify the commutative law under addition

Verify the commutative law under addition for whole numbers 23 and 27.

Step 1: By the commutative law of addition: 23 + 27 = 27 + 23.

Step 2: Take L.H.S = 23 + 27 = 50.

Step 3: Now take R.H.S = 27 + 23 = 50.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S, so 23 + 27 = 27 + 23.

Final answer: Hence, the commutative law of addition is verified.

Associative law of addition

According to this law of addition, changing the "grouping" of addends does not change the sum. For example, (4 + 5) + 7 = 4 + (5 + 7), that is, 9 + 7 = 4 + 12, so 16 = 16.

Did You Know? The sum of zero (0) and an integer is the same as that integer. For example, 0 + 7 = 7 or 7 + 0 = 7, and the number '0' is called additive identity.

Book Example 13 — Verify the associative law of addition

(i) For the integers 15, −16 and 19.

Step 1: By the associative law: (15 − 16) + 19 = 15 + (−16 + 19).

Step 2: Take L.H.S = (15 − 16) + 19 = −1 + 19 = 18.

Step 3: Now take R.H.S = 15 + (−16 + 19) = 15 + 3 = 18.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the associative law of addition is verified.

(ii) For the integers −14, −18 and 23.

Step 1: By the associative law: (−14 − 18) + 23 = −14 + (−18 + 23).

Step 2: Take L.H.S = (−14 − 18) + 23 = −32 + 23 = −9.

Step 3: Now take R.H.S = −14 + (−18 + 23) = −14 + 5 = −9.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the associative law of addition is verified.

Practice-6

(i) Verify the commutative law for the integers −49 and 57.

Step 1: By the commutative law of addition: −49 + 57 = 57 + (−49).

Step 2: Take L.H.S = −49 + 57 = 8.

Step 3: Take R.H.S = 57 + (−49) = 57 − 49 = 8.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the commutative law is verified for −49 and 57.

(ii) Verify the associative law for the integers −17, 43 and 64.

Step 1: By the associative law of addition: (−17 + 43) + 64 = −17 + (43 + 64).

Step 2: Take L.H.S = (−17 + 43) + 64 = 26 + 64 = 90.

Step 3: Take R.H.S = −17 + (43 + 64) = −17 + 107 = 90.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the associative law is verified for −17, 43 and 64.

Worked examples — Exercise 3.1

Q1. Use a number line to simplify the following (the number-line movement is described in words in each step):

(i) (+7) + (+9)

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 7 steps towards the right, reaching at +7.

Step 2: Move 9 more steps towards the right.

Final answer: (+7) + (+9) = +16.

(ii) 0 + (−10)

Step 1: Start at 0. Adding 0 keeps us at 0.

Step 2: Adding −10 means moving 10 steps towards the left.

Final answer: 0 + (−10) = −10.

(iii) (−8) + (−6)

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 8 steps towards the left, reaching at −8.

Step 2: Move 6 more steps towards the left.

Final answer: (−8) + (−6) = −14.

(iv) (+17) − (+8)

Step 1: Subtraction is the inverse process of addition: (+17) − (+8) = 17 − 8.

Step 2: Start at 17 on the number line and move 8 steps back towards the left.

Final answer: (+17) − (+8) = +9.

(v) (+11) + 0

Step 1: Start at +11 on the number line.

Step 2: Adding 0 (the additive identity) does not move us; the integer remains the same.

Final answer: (+11) + 0 = +11.

(vi) (+13) + (+18) + (+8)

Step 1: Start at 0, move 13 steps right to +13, then 18 more steps right to +31.

Step 2: Move 8 more steps towards the right: 31 + 8 = 39.

Final answer: (+13) + (+18) + (+8) = +39.

(vii) (+15) + (−3) + (−5)

Step 1: Start at 0 and move 15 steps towards the right, reaching at +15.

Step 2: Adding −3 moves us 3 steps left to 12; adding −5 moves us 5 more steps left to 7.

Final answer: (+15) + (−3) + (−5) = +7.

(viii) (−8) − (−9)

Step 1: Change the sign of the integer to be subtracted: (−8) − (−9) = −8 + 9.

Step 2: Start at −8 on the number line and move 9 steps towards the right.

Final answer: (−8) − (−9) = +1.

(ix) 7 − (−8)

Step 1: Change the sign of the integer to be subtracted: 7 − (−8) = 7 + 8.

Step 2: Start at 7 on the number line and move 8 steps towards the right.

Final answer: 7 − (−8) = +15.

Q2. Use a number line to find the difference of the following integers (subtraction is done by the rule: change the sign of the integer to be subtracted and add according to the rules of addition):

(i) (+17) − (+11)

Step 1: (+17) − (+11) = 17 − 11.

Step 2: 17 − 11 = 6.

Final answer: +6.

(ii) (−34) − (+16)

Step 1: Change the sign of (+16): −34 − 16.

Step 2: Add the two negative values and keep the negative sign: − (34 + 16) = −50.

Final answer: −50.

(iii) (+2) − (−4)

Step 1: Change the sign of (−4): 2 + 4.

Step 2: 2 + 4 = 6.

Final answer: +6.

(iv) (−94) − (−19)

Step 1: Change the sign of (−19): −94 + 19.

Step 2: Subtract and keep the sign of the greater value: − (94 − 19) = −75.

Final answer: −75.

(v) (−8) − (−3)

Step 1: Change the sign of (−3): −8 + 3.

Step 2: − (8 − 3) = −5.

Final answer: −5.

(vi) (−81) − (+16)

Step 1: Change the sign of (+16): −81 − 16.

Step 2: − (81 + 16) = −97.

Final answer: −97.

(vii) (+12) − (+10)

Step 1: (+12) − (+10) = 12 − 10.

Step 2: 12 − 10 = 2.

Final answer: +2.

(viii) (−9) − (−4)

Step 1: Change the sign of (−4): −9 + 4.

Step 2: − (9 − 4) = −5.

Final answer: −5.

(ix) 47 − 18

Step 1: Both are positive; subtract the smaller from the greater: 47 − 18.

Step 2: 47 − 18 = 29.

Final answer: 29.

Q3. Verify the associative law of addition for the integers 17, −21 and 25.

Step 1: By the associative law of addition: (17 + (−21)) + 25 = 17 + ((−21) + 25).

Step 2: Take L.H.S = (17 − 21) + 25 = −4 + 25 = 21.

Step 3: Take R.H.S = 17 + (−21 + 25) = 17 + 4 = 21.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S = 21.

Final answer: Hence, the associative law of addition is verified for 17, −21 and 25.

Q4. The sum of two integers is −107. One of them is −49; find the other.

Step 1: The other integer = sum − given integer = −107 − (−49).

Step 2: Change the sign of the integer to be subtracted: −107 + 49.

Step 3: Subtract and keep the sign of the greater value: − (107 − 49) = −58.

Step 4: Check: −49 + (−58) = −107, which is the given sum.

Final answer: The other integer is −58.

Q5. Verify the commutative property of addition for 39 and −51.

Step 1: By the commutative law of addition: 39 + (−51) = (−51) + 39.

Step 2: Take L.H.S = 39 + (−51) = 39 − 51 = −12.

Step 3: Take R.H.S = (−51) + 39 = −51 + 39 = −12.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the commutative property of addition is verified for 39 and −51.

Q6. The difference between two integers is 48; one of them is 14. Find the other.

Step 1: While subtracting, write the greater integer first. Let the other integer be the greater one: other − 14 = 48.

Step 2: So the other integer = 48 + 14 = 62.

Step 3: Check: 62 − 14 = 48, which is the given difference.

Final answer: The other integer is 62.

Q7. Two orange trains left Samanabad station at the same time. One travelled 14 km towards Ali Town, while the other travelled 10 km towards Dera Gujran in the opposite direction. Find the total distance between both trains.

Step 1: Distance travelled by the first train from the station = 14 km.

Step 2: Distance travelled by the second train from the station, in the opposite direction = 10 km.

Step 3: As the trains moved in opposite directions, the total distance between them = 14 + 10 = 24 km.

Final answer: The total distance between both trains is 24 km.

mcqs.q: According to the commutative law of addition, the sum of two integers remains unchanged by changing what?
mcqs.why: The commutative law of addition says the sum remains unchanged by changing the order, for example 2 + 3 = 3 + 2.

mcqs.q: In the example 2 + 3 = 3 + 2, what is the common value of both sides?
mcqs.why: Working out both sides: 2 + 3 = 5 and 3 + 2 = 5, so both sides are equal to 5, which verifies the law.

mcqs.q: Does the commutative law hold for subtraction?
options: No, because 8 - 3 is not equal to 3 - 8
mcqs.why: The notes state the commutative law does not hold for subtraction: 8 - 3 = 5 but 3 - 8 = -5, and 5 is not equal to -5.

mcqs.q: To verify the commutative law for 23 and 27, what is 23 + 27?
mcqs.why: L.H.S = 23 + 27 = 50 and R.H.S = 27 + 23 = 50; since L.H.S = R.H.S, the commutative law is verified.

mcqs.q: According to the associative law of addition, changing what does not change the sum?
mcqs.why: The associative law of addition says changing the grouping of addends does not change the sum, as shown by (4 + 5) + 7 = 4 + (5 + 7).

mcqs.q: What is (4 + 5) + 7, which also equals 4 + (5 + 7)?
mcqs.why: L.H.S = (4 + 5) + 7 = 9 + 7 = 16, and R.H.S = 4 + (5 + 7) = 4 + 12 = 16, so both groupings give 16.

mcqs.q: Which number is called the additive identity?
mcqs.why: The sum of zero and an integer is the same integer, for example 0 + 7 = 7 or 7 + 0 = 7, so 0 is called the additive identity.

mcqs.q: Using the associative law, what is (15 + (-16)) + 19?
Using the associative law, what is (-14 + (-18)) + 23?
To verify the commutative law for -49 and 57, what is -49 + 57?
mcqs.why: L.H.S = -49 + 57 = 8, and R.H.S = 57 + (-49) = 57 - 49 = 8; since both sides are equal, the law is verified.

lessons.title: 3.4.1 Multiplication of Integers
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplication and division of integers

We have learnt about the multiplication and division of two or more numbers in our previous classes. Now in this section we will learn multiplication and division of two or more integers.

Multiplication of Integers

As we are familiar, multiplication is the shortest form of repeated addition. For example, (+5) × (+2): multiplying (+5) with (+2) means five jumps, each jump is two steps in the same direction.

Step 1: (a) Five jumps, each jump is of two steps, take us from 0 to +10 on the number line.

Step 2: Hence, (+5) × (+2) = +10.

Step 3: (b) Two jumps, each jump is of five steps, also take us from 0 to +10.

Final answer: (+2) × (+5) = +10.

Multiplication of two integers with like signs

When we multiply two integers having the "same" signs (both positive or both negative), then the product of these integers is a positive integer. Remember: When we multiply an even number of integers with the same sign, the product is always positive.

Note: In order to draw a large number on the number line, we need to fix a scale on the number line with equal intervals. For example, if we take the distance between two points equal to 50, then 1 unit = 1 × 50 = 50 and 7 units = 7 × 50 = 350.

Book Example 14 — Solve using the number line

(i) (+3) × (+6)

Step 1: Multiplying (+3) with (+6) means three jumps, each jump is six steps in the same direction.

Step 2: The three jumps take us from 0 to +18 on the number line.

Final answer: (+3) × (+6) = +18.

(ii) (−6) × (−2)

Step 1: Multiplying (−6) with (−2) means six jumps, each jump is two steps in the opposite direction of −6.

Step 2: The six jumps take us from 0 to +12 on the number line; the product of two integers with like (negative) signs is positive.

Final answer: (−6) × (−2) = +12.

Multiplication of two integers with unlike signs

When we multiply two integers having "different" signs (one positive and the other negative), the product of these integers is a negative integer.

Rules for multiplication: (+) × (+) = + ; (+) × (−) = − ; (−) × (+) = − ; (−) × (−) = +.

Book Example 15 — Solve using the number line

(i) (−3) × (+6)

Step 1: Multiplying (−3) with (+6) means three jumps, each jump is of six steps in the same direction of (−3).

Step 2: The three jumps take us from 0 to −18 on the number line.

Final answer: (−3) × (+6) = −18.

(ii) (+5) × (−3)

Step 1: Multiplying (+5) with (−3) means five jumps, each jump is of three steps in the same direction of (−3).

Step 2: The five jumps take us from 0 to −15 on the number line.

Final answer: (+5) × (−3) = −15.

Book Example 16 — Find the product without using the number line

(i) (+23) and (+22)

Step 1: Like signs give a positive product: (+23) × (+22) = + (23 × 22).

Step 2: 23 × 22 = 506.

Final answer: +506.

(ii) (−8) and (−15)

Step 1: Like signs give a positive product: (−8) × (−15) = + (8 × 15).

Step 2: 8 × 15 = 120.

Final answer: +120.

(iii) (+24) and (−10)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative product: (+24) × (−10) = − (24 × 10).

Step 2: 24 × 10 = 240.

Final answer: −240.

(iv) (−36) and (+11)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative product: (−36) × (+11) = − (36 × 11).

Step 2: 36 × 11 = 396.

Final answer: −396.

Practice-6 — Multiply

(i) 10 by −12

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative product: 10 × (−12) = − (10 × 12).

Step 2: 10 × 12 = 120.

Final answer: −120.

(ii) 14 by −9

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative product: 14 × (−9) = − (14 × 9).

Step 2: 14 × 9 = 126.

Final answer: −126.

(iii) 34 by 8

Step 1: Like signs give a positive product: 34 × 8.

Step 2: 34 × 8 = 272.

Final answer: 272.

(iv) −16 by 10

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative product: (−16) × 10 = − (16 × 10).

Step 2: 16 × 10 = 160.

Final answer: −160.

mcqs.q: Multiplication is the shortest form of which process?
mcqs.why: The notes state that multiplication is the shortest form of repeated addition, shown by jumps of equal steps on the number line.

mcqs.q: What is (+5) x (+2)?
mcqs.why: Multiplying (+5) by (+2) means five jumps of two steps in the same direction: 5 x 2 = 10, so the product is +10.

mcqs.q: When two integers with like signs are multiplied, the product is always what?
mcqs.why: The notes state that when we multiply two integers having the same signs, both positive or both negative, the product is a positive integer.

mcqs.q: Using the number line, what is (+3) x (+6)?
mcqs.why: Multiplying (+3) by (+6) means three jumps of six steps in the same direction: 3 x 6 = 18, so the product is +18.

mcqs.q: What is (-6) x (-2)?
mcqs.why: Both integers have like negative signs, so the product is positive: 6 x 2 = 12, therefore (-6) x (-2) = +12.

mcqs.q: When two integers with unlike signs are multiplied, the product is always what?
options: The same as the first integer
mcqs.why: The multiplication rules in the notes are (+) x (-) = - and (-) x (+) = -, so unlike signs always give a negative product.

mcqs.q: Using the number line, what is (-3) x (+6)?
mcqs.why: The signs are unlike, so the product is negative: -(3 x 6) = -18, from three jumps of six steps in the direction of -3.

mcqs.q: What is (+5) x (-3)?
mcqs.why: The signs are unlike, so the product is negative: -(5 x 3) = -15, from five jumps of three steps in the direction of -3.

mcqs.q: Without using a number line, what is (+23) x (+22)?
mcqs.why: Like signs give a positive product: 23 x 22 = 23 x 20 + 23 x 2 = 460 + 46 = 506, so the answer is +506.

mcqs.q: Without using a number line, what is (-8) x (-15)?
mcqs.why: Like signs give a positive product: 8 x 15 = 120, so (-8) x (-15) = +120, as worked out in the book example.

lessons.title: 3.4.2 Division of Integers
lessons.notes_html:
Division of Integers

Division of integers is same as the division of whole numbers. The procedure for dividing integers is same as we used for multiplying the integers. "The division is the inverse process of multiplication." For example, 7 × 6 = 42 gives 42 ÷ 6 = 7 and 42 ÷ 7 = 6, with the same numbers.

In an expression such as (+63) ÷ (+9) = (+7): (+63) is the Dividend, (+9) is the Divisor and (+7) is the Quotient.

Division of two integers with like signs

Since division is an inverse process of multiplication, the division of an integer (dividend) by another given integer (divisor) means to find an integer (quotient) which when multiplied by the given integer (divisor) will give the dividend. Like signs give a positive quotient.

Book Example 17 — Workout

(i) (+45) ÷ (+5)

Step 1: Write the division as multiplication by the reciprocal: (+45) ÷ (+5) = (+45) × (+1/5).

Step 2: As (+) × (+) = (+), the quotient is positive: + (45/5).

Step 3: 45 ÷ 5 = 9.

Final answer: (+45) ÷ (+5) = +9.

(ii) (−54) ÷ (−6)

Step 1: Write (−54) ÷ (−6) = (−54) × (−1/6).

Step 2: As (−) × (−) = (+), the quotient is positive: + (54/6).

Step 3: 54 ÷ 6 = 9.

Final answer: (−54) ÷ (−6) = +9.

Practice-6 — Divide

(i) −48 ÷ 6

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative quotient: − (48 ÷ 6).

Step 2: 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

Final answer: −8.

(ii) 130 ÷ (−5)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative quotient: − (130 ÷ 5).

Step 2: 130 ÷ 5 = 26.

Final answer: −26.

(iii) −216 ÷ (−4)

Step 1: Like signs give a positive quotient: + (216 ÷ 4).

Step 2: 216 ÷ 4 = 54.

Final answer: 54.

(iv) 105 ÷ 7

Step 1: Like signs give a positive quotient: 105 ÷ 7.

Step 2: 105 ÷ 7 = 15.

Final answer: 15.

Division of two integers with unlike signs

To divide (+70) by (−10) means to find an integer such as (−7) which when multiplied by (−10) will give (+70), i.e. (−10) × (−7) = (+70). So, (+70) ÷ (−10) = (−7): unlike signs give a negative quotient.

Book Example 18 — Solve

(i) (+195) ÷ (−5)

Step 1: Write (+195) ÷ (−5) = (+195) × (−1/5). As (+) × (−) = (−), the quotient is negative: − (195/5).

Step 2: 195 ÷ 5 = 39.

Final answer: (+195) ÷ (−5) = −39.

(ii) (−80) ÷ (+8)

Step 1: Write (−80) ÷ (+8) = (−80) × (+1/8). As (−) × (+) = (−), the quotient is negative: − (80/8).

Step 2: 80 ÷ 8 = 10.

Final answer: (−80) ÷ (+8) = −10.

Division of an integer by zero (0)

Division of any number by zero (0) never comes to an end at any stage and we cannot find the answer. For example, dividing 8 by 0 in the long division leaves the remainder 8 again and again. But no value works for 0 times, because multiplication of any number with '0' is '0'. Therefore, the division of an integer by zero is not possible.

Remember: Zero (0) is an integer, neither positive nor negative. When it is divided by any integer, the quotient is zero. But dividing any other integer by zero is undefined.

mcqs.q: Division of integers is the inverse process of which operation?
mcqs.why: The notes state that division is the inverse process of multiplication. For example, 7 x 6 = 42 gives back 42 / 6 = 7 and 42 / 7 = 6 with the same numbers.
The notes name the parts of this division: (+63) is the dividend (the number being divided), (+9) is the divisor and (+7) is the quotient.
Working: write the division as (+45) x (+1/5). Like signs (+) x (+) give a positive result, and 45 / 5 = 9, so (+45) / (+5) = +9.
Working: write it as (-54) x (-1/6). Like signs (-) x (-) give a positive quotient, and 54 / 6 = 9, so (-54) / (-6) = +9.

mcqs.q: What is -48 / 6?
mcqs.why: Working: the signs are unlike, so the quotient is negative: -(48 / 6). Since 48 / 6 = 8, the answer is -8.
Working: both integers have like (negative) signs, so the quotient is positive: +(216 / 4). Since 216 / 4 = 54, the answer is 54.
Working: we need the integer which multiplied by (-10) gives (+70). Since (-10) x (-7) = +70, the quotient is -7; unlike signs also give a negative quotient.
Working: write it as (+195) x (-1/5). Unlike signs (+) x (-) give a negative quotient: -(195 / 5). Since 195 / 5 = 39, the answer is -39.

mcqs.q: Zero (0) divided by any integer gives what quotient?
mcqs.why: The notes say zero is an integer, neither positive nor negative, and when zero is divided by any integer the quotient is zero, because 0 times any integer is 0.

mcqs.q: What is the result of dividing an integer such as 8 by zero (0)?
mcqs.why: Dividing 8 by 0 never ends: the remainder stays 8 again and again, and no value works because any number multiplied by 0 gives 0, never 8. So division by zero is not possible.

lessons.title: 3.5 VERIFICATION OF COMMUTATIVE, ASSOCIATIVE AND DISTRIBUTIVE LAWS
lessons.notes_html:
Verification of commutative, associative and distributive laws

The following laws of multiplication of integers are true.

Commutative law of multiplication

According to this law of multiplication, the product of two integers remains unchanged by changing their "order". For example, 6 × 5 = 5 × 6, that is, 30 = 30.

Remember: Commutative law of division of integers is not true, e.g. 3 ÷ 2 ≠ 2 ÷ 3.

Book Example 19 — Verify the commutative law under multiplication

Verify the commutative law under multiplication for 24 and 28.

Step 1: By the commutative law of multiplication: 24 × 28 = 28 × 24.

Step 2: Take L.H.S = 24 × 28 = 672.

Step 3: Take R.H.S = 28 × 24 = 672.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S, so 24 × 28 = 28 × 24.

Final answer: Hence, the commutative law of multiplication is verified.

Associative law of multiplication

According to this law of multiplication, "changing grouping" of the factors does not change the product. For example, (4 × 5) × 7 = 4 × (5 × 7), that is, 20 × 7 = 4 × 35, so 140 = 140.

Book Example 20 — Verify the associative law

Verify the associative law for −6, 7 and 8.

Step 1: By the associative law of multiplication we need to verify: (−6 × 7) × 8 = −6 × (7 × 8).

Step 2: Take L.H.S = (−6 × 7) × 8 = −42 × 8 = −336.

Step 3: Take R.H.S = −6 × (7 × 8) = −6 × 56 = −336.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the associative law of multiplication is verified.

Distributive law of multiplication

According to this law of multiplication, "multiplying a number by the group of numbers added together is same as doing each multiplication separately." For example, with 4 rows of 2 apples and 3 mangoes: 4 × (2 + 3) = 4 × 2 + 4 × 3, that is, 4 × 5 = 8 + 12, so 20 = 20.

Book Example 21 — Verify the distributive law of multiplication

Verify the distributive law of multiplication for −10 × (7 + 13) = (−10 × 7) + (−10 × 13).

Step 1: Take L.H.S = −10 × (7 + 13) = −10 × 20 = −200.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = (−10 × 7) + (−10 × 13) = −70 − 130 = −200.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the distributive law is verified.

Did You Know? The integer "1" has a special role in multiplication just as the number "0" has in case of addition. "The product of '1' and an integer is the same as that number." For example, 1 × 13 = 13 or 13 × 1 = 13, and the number 1 is known as multiplicative identity.

Practice-8

(i) Verify the commutative law for integers 105 and −301.

Step 1: By the commutative law of multiplication: 105 × (−301) = (−301) × 105.

Step 2: Take L.H.S = 105 × (−301) = −31,605.

Step 3: Take R.H.S = (−301) × 105 = −31,605.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the commutative law is verified for 105 and −301.

(ii) Verify the associative law of multiplication for integers −7, −13, −15.

Step 1: By the associative law: (−7 × −13) × −15 = −7 × (−13 × −15).

Step 2: Take L.H.S = (−7 × −13) × −15 = 91 × −15 = −1365.

Step 3: Take R.H.S = −7 × (−13 × −15) = −7 × 195 = −1365.

Step 4: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the associative law of multiplication is verified for −7, −13, −15.

(iii) Verify the distributive law: −15 × (8 − 7) = (−15 × 8) + (−15 × −7).

Step 1: Take L.H.S = −15 × (8 − 7) = −15 × 1 = −15.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = (−15 × 8) + (−15 × −7) = −120 + 105 = −15.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Hence, the distributive law is verified.

Worked examples — Exercise 3.2

Q1. Find the product of the following integers using a number line (multiplication is repeated addition; the jumps are described in words):

(i) +4 and +5

Step 1: (+4) × (+5) means four jumps of 5 steps to the right, or five jumps of 4 steps to the right.

Step 2: Like signs give a positive product: 4 × 5 = 20.

Final answer: +20.

(ii) −3 and +8

Step 1: (−3) × (+8) means three jumps of 8 steps in the direction of −3, that is, to the left.

Step 2: Unlike signs give a negative product: − (3 × 8) = −24.

Final answer: −24.

(iii) 0 and −6

Step 1: Any number of jumps of 0 steps, or 0 jumps, stay at 0.

Final answer: 0.

(iv) +11 and −2

Step 1: (+11) × (−2) means eleven jumps of 2 steps in the direction of −2, that is, to the left.

Step 2: Unlike signs give a negative product: − (11 × 2) = −22.

Final answer: −22.

(v) +5 and −5

Step 1: (+5) × (−5) means five jumps of 5 steps to the left.

Step 2: Unlike signs give a negative product: − (5 × 5) = −25.

Final answer: −25.

(vi) −10 and −3

Step 1: (−10) × (−3) means ten jumps of 3 steps in the opposite direction of −10, that is, to the right.

Step 2: Like signs give a positive product: + (10 × 3) = +30.

Final answer: +30.

(vii) +9 and 0

Step 1: Multiplying any integer by 0 gives 0; the jumps are of 0 steps.

Final answer: 0.

(viii) 2 and −7

Step 1: 2 × (−7) means two jumps of 7 steps to the left.

Step 2: Unlike signs give a negative product: − (2 × 7) = −14.

Final answer: −14.

Q2. Solve:

(i) (+38) × (−23)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative product: − (38 × 23).

Step 2: 38 × 23 = 874.

Final answer: −874.

(ii) (+24) × (+15)

Step 1: Like signs give a positive product: + (24 × 15).

Step 2: 24 × 15 = 360.

Final answer: +360.

(iii) (−15) × (−19)

Step 1: Like signs give a positive product: + (15 × 19).

Step 2: 15 × 19 = 285.

Final answer: 285.

(iv) (+23) × (−41)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative product: − (23 × 41).

Step 2: 23 × 41 = 943.

Final answer: −943.

(v) (+74) × (+0)

Step 1: The product of any integer with 0 is 0.

Final answer: 0.

(vi) (−89) × (−1)

Step 1: Like signs give a positive product: + (89 × 1).

Step 2: 89 × 1 = 89 (1 is the multiplicative identity).

Final answer: +89.

Q3. Find the quotient:

(i) (+51) ÷ (+3)

Step 1: Like signs give a positive quotient: + (51 ÷ 3).

Step 2: 51 ÷ 3 = 17.

Final answer: +17.

(ii) (27) ÷ (−3)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative quotient: − (27 ÷ 3).

Step 2: 27 ÷ 3 = 9.

Final answer: −9.

(iii) (−54) ÷ (+9)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative quotient: − (54 ÷ 9).

Step 2: 54 ÷ 9 = 6.

Final answer: −6.

(iv) (−78) ÷ (−13)

Step 1: Like signs give a positive quotient: + (78 ÷ 13).

Step 2: 78 ÷ 13 = 6.

Final answer: +6.

(v) (+108) ÷ (−1)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative quotient: − (108 ÷ 1).

Step 2: 108 ÷ 1 = 108.

Final answer: −108.

(vi) (+156) ÷ 0

Step 1: Division of an integer by zero (0) is not possible, because no number multiplied by 0 gives 156.

Final answer: Undefined.

(vii) 0 ÷ (+89)

Step 1: Zero divided by any integer gives the quotient zero, because 0 × 89 = 0.

Final answer: 0.

(viii) (+1) × (−228) (printed with the × sign in this quotient question)

Step 1: Unlike signs give a negative result: − (1 × 228).

Step 2: 1 × 228 = 228 (1 is the multiplicative identity).

Final answer: −228.

Q4. Fill in the blanks with an appropriate integer:

(i) (____) × (+7) = (−56)

Step 1: The product is negative, so the missing integer is negative: 56 ÷ 7 = 8 with a negative sign.

Step 2: Check: (−8) × (+7) = −56.

Final answer: −8.

(ii) (−3) × (____) = 30

Step 1: The product is positive while −3 is negative, so the missing integer is negative: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 with a negative sign.

Step 2: Check: (−3) × (−10) = 30.

Final answer: −10.

(iii) (−21) ÷ (____) = −3

Step 1: The quotient is negative and the dividend is negative, so the divisor is positive: 21 ÷ 3 = 7.

Step 2: Check: (−21) ÷ 7 = −3.

Final answer: 7.

(iv) (____) ÷ (+12) = 60

Step 1: The dividend = quotient × divisor = 60 × 12 = 720.

Step 2: Check: 720 ÷ (+12) = 60.

Final answer: 720.

(v) (+121) × (____) = 0

Step 1: A product is 0 only when one factor is 0.

Step 2: Check: (+121) × 0 = 0.

Final answer: 0.

(vi) (−212) ÷ (____) = (−212)

Step 1: An integer divided by 1 gives the same integer (1 is the multiplicative identity).

Step 2: Check: (−212) ÷ 1 = (−212).

Final answer: 1.

Q5. Verify the following (commutative law of addition):

(i) 5 + 8 = 8 + 5

Step 1: Take L.H.S = 5 + 8 = 13.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = 8 + 5 = 13.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Verified: 13 = 13.

(ii) 29 + 13 = 13 + 29

Step 1: Take L.H.S = 29 + 13 = 42.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = 13 + 29 = 42.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Verified: 42 = 42.

(iii) 231 + 145 = 145 + 231

Step 1: Take L.H.S = 231 + 145 = 376.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = 145 + 231 = 376.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Verified: 376 = 376.

Q6. Verify the commutative law under addition for the following whole numbers:

(i) 29 and 39

Step 1: 29 + 39 = 68.

Step 2: 39 + 29 = 68. As both sums are equal.

Final answer: Verified: 29 + 39 = 39 + 29 = 68.

(ii) 348 and 289

Step 1: 348 + 289 = 637.

Step 2: 289 + 348 = 637. As both sums are equal.

Final answer: Verified: 348 + 289 = 289 + 348 = 637.

(iii) 828 and 215

Step 1: 828 + 215 = 1043.

Step 2: 215 + 828 = 1043. As both sums are equal.

Final answer: Verified: 828 + 215 = 215 + 828 = 1043.

(iv) 3335 and 411

Step 1: 3335 + 411 = 3746.

Step 2: 411 + 3335 = 3746. As both sums are equal.

Final answer: Verified: 3335 + 411 = 411 + 3335 = 3746.

Q7. Verify (associative law of multiplication):

(i) −5 × (−7 × 8) = (−5 × −7) × 8

Step 1: Take L.H.S = −5 × (−7 × 8) = −5 × (−56) = 280.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = (−5 × −7) × 8 = 35 × 8 = 280.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Verified: 280 = 280.

(ii) −9 × (−10 × −7) = (−9 × −10) × −7

Step 1: Take L.H.S = −9 × (−10 × −7) = −9 × 70 = −630.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = (−9 × −10) × −7 = 90 × −7 = −630.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Verified: −630 = −630.

Q8. Verify the distributive law:

(i) 7 × (8 + 9) = 7 × 8 + 7 × 9

Step 1: Take L.H.S = 7 × (8 + 9) = 7 × 17 = 119.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = 7 × 8 + 7 × 9 = 56 + 63 = 119.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Verified: 119 = 119.

(ii) 10 × (30 − 20) = 10 × 30 − 10 × 20

Step 1: Take L.H.S = 10 × (30 − 20) = 10 × 10 = 100.

Step 2: Take R.H.S = 10 × 30 − 10 × 20 = 300 − 200 = 100.

Step 3: As L.H.S = R.H.S.

Final answer: Verified: 100 = 100.

Q9. The sum of two integers is 194. One of them is −28. Find the other integer.

Step 1: The other integer = sum − given integer = 194 − (−28).

Step 2: Change the sign of the integer to be subtracted: 194 + 28 = 222.

Step 3: Check: 222 + (−28) = 194, the given sum.

Final answer: The other integer is 222.

Q10. Rabia asked her mother to hold her savings. At the start of July her saving was Rs. 100. At the end of July she added Rs. 250 more in her savings. In the month of August she borrowed Rs. 185 to spend. What is the remaining or owed amount?

Step 1: Savings at the start of July = Rs. 100.

Step 2: After adding Rs. 250: 100 + 250 = Rs. 350.

Step 3: After borrowing (spending) Rs. 185: 350 − 185 = Rs. 165.

Final answer: The remaining amount is Rs. 165.

Q11. On Sunday morning the temperature of Faisalabad city was 45°C. It dropped 3°C per hour due to weather conditions. What was the total change in temperature after 5 hours?

Step 1: Drop in temperature in 1 hour = 3°C.

Step 2: Total drop in 5 hours = 5 × 3°C = 15°C.

Step 3: Temperature after 5 hours = 45°C − 15°C = 30°C.

Final answer: The total change is a drop of 15°C, and the temperature after 5 hours is 30°C.

mcqs.q: According to the commutative law of multiplication, the product of two integers remains unchanged by changing their what?
mcqs.why: The commutative law of multiplication says the product remains unchanged by changing the order of the integers, for example 6 x 5 = 5 x 6 = 30.

mcqs.q: To verify the commutative law for 24 and 28, what is 24 x 28?
mcqs.why: Working: L.H.S = 24 x 28 = 672. R.H.S = 28 x 24 = 672. Since L.H.S = R.H.S, the commutative law of multiplication is verified for 24 and 28.

mcqs.q: Does the commutative law hold for division of integers?
options: Only when both numbers are equal
No, for example 3 / 2 is not equal to 2 / 3
mcqs.why: The notes clearly state that the commutative law of division of integers is not true, giving the example 3 / 2 != 2 / 3, because changing the order changes the result.

mcqs.q: According to the associative law of multiplication, changing what does not change the product?
mcqs.why: The associative law of multiplication says that changing the grouping of the factors does not change the product, for example (4 x 5) x 7 = 4 x (5 x 7).

mcqs.q: What is (4 x 5) x 7, grouped the other way as 4 x (5 x 7)?
mcqs.why: Working: (4 x 5) x 7 = 20 x 7 = 140, and 4 x (5 x 7) = 4 x 35 = 140. Both groupings give 140, which verifies the associative law.

mcqs.q: Using the associative law, what is (-6 x 7) x 8?
mcqs.why: Working: L.H.S = (-6 x 7) x 8 = -42 x 8 = -336. Check the other grouping: -6 x (7 x 8) = -6 x 56 = -336. Both sides are equal.

mcqs.q: The distributive law says that multiplying a number by a group of numbers added together is the same as what?
options: Adding the number to each one
Dividing the number by each one
Changing the order of the numbers
mcqs.why: By the distributive law, multiplying a number by the group of numbers added together is the same as doing each multiplication separately, e.g. 4 x (2 + 3) = 4 x 2 + 4 x 3.

mcqs.q: Using the distributive law, what is 4 x (2 + 3)?
mcqs.why: Working: L.H.S = 4 x (2 + 3) = 4 x 5 = 20. R.H.S = 4 x 2 + 4 x 3 = 8 + 12 = 20. Both sides are equal, so the answer is 20.

mcqs.q: What is -10 x (7 + 13)?
mcqs.why: Working: L.H.S = -10 x (7 + 13) = -10 x 20 = -200. By the distributive law: (-10 x 7) + (-10 x 13) = -70 - 130 = -200. Both give -200.

mcqs.q: Which integer is called the multiplicative identity?
mcqs.why: The product of 1 and an integer is the same as that number, for example 1 x 13 = 13 or 13 x 1 = 13, so the number 1 is known as the multiplicative identity.

lessons.title: 3.5.1 Different kinds of Brackets
lessons.notes_html:
The order of mathematical operations (BODMAS rule)

We are familiar with simplification of expressions from our previous classes. In routine life we add, multiply, subtract or divide two or more numbers for different purposes. After doing these we get our result in simplified form. "The process of getting a simplified number is known as simplification."

To simplify a mathematical expression with two or more operations we use the BODMAS rule. The letters of BODMAS are used for the order of operations which helps us to simplify the given expressions. The order of operations is used in the field of Mathematics, Science, Technology and many computer programming languages.

For example, at the start of this sub-domain two students solved 5 + 3 × 4 ÷ 2 in different ways: Student-1 did 5 + 3 × 4 ÷ 2 = 5 + 3 × 2 = 5 + 6 = 11, while Student-2 did 5 + 3 × 4 ÷ 2 = 8 × 4 ÷ 2 = 32 ÷ 2 = 16. Student-1 is doing well, because multiplication and division are done before addition.

Book example — Naseem's eggs

Naseem has 30 eggs in each of six egg trays. Seven other trays have 12 eggs in each tray. How many eggs does Naseem have in all?

Step 1: Eggs in the six trays = 6 × 30, and eggs in the seven trays = 7 × 12. Total number of eggs = 6 × 30 + 7 × 12.

Step 2: Do the multiplications first: 6 × 30 = 180 and 7 × 12 = 84.

Step 3: Add: 180 + 84 = 264.

Final answer: Naseem has 264 eggs in all.

For a numerical expression like 5 × (45 ÷ 7) − (18 ÷ 3) + 8, we use the BODMAS rule to simplify.

Different kinds of Brackets

Brackets are the symbols which are used in pairs to group two or more numbers together with mathematical operations. There are four kinds of brackets that are mentioned below:

  • (i) Bar or vinculum: "——"
  • (ii) Parentheses or curved brackets or round brackets: "( )"
  • (iii) Braces or curly bracket: "{ }"
  • (iv) Square brackets or box brackets: "[ ]"

mcqs.q: The process of getting a simplified number from an expression is known as what?
mcqs.why: The notes define it directly: the process of getting a simplified number is known as simplification, which we do when we add, multiply, subtract or divide numbers for different purposes.

mcqs.q: To simplify a mathematical expression with two or more operations, which rule do we use?
mcqs.why: The notes state that to simplify a mathematical expression with two or more operations we use the BODMAS rule, whose letters give the order of operations.

mcqs.q: What is the correct value of 5 + 3 x 4 / 2?
mcqs.why: Working: multiplication and division are done before addition. Step 1: 3 x 4 / 2 = 12 / 2 = 6 (or 4 / 2 = 2, then 3 x 2 = 6). Step 2: 5 + 6 = 11.

mcqs.q: In 5 + 3 x 4 / 2, why is the answer 11 and not 16?
options: Because addition is always done first
Because the numbers are added from right to left
Because multiplication and division are done before addition
mcqs.why: Student-1 got 11 by doing multiplication and division before addition, which is correct. Student-2 added 5 + 3 first and got 16, which is wrong under the order of operations.

mcqs.q: Naseem has 30 eggs in each of six trays and 12 eggs in each of seven other trays. How many eggs does she have in all?
mcqs.why: Working: total = 6 x 30 + 7 x 12. Do the multiplications first: 6 x 30 = 180 and 7 x 12 = 84. Then add: 180 + 84 = 264 eggs.

mcqs.q: In Naseem's egg problem, 6 x 30 + 7 x 12, which operations are done first?
mcqs.why: Working: by the order of operations the multiplications are done first: 6 x 30 = 180 and 7 x 12 = 84, and only then are the results added: 180 + 84 = 264.

mcqs.q: The bar bracket is also called what?
mcqs.why: The notes list four kinds of brackets, and the first kind, the bar drawn over numbers, is called the bar or vinculum, shown as a line over the grouped numbers.

mcqs.q: Parentheses ( ) are also called what?
mcqs.why: The notes name the second kind of brackets, ( ), as parentheses or curved brackets or round brackets, used in pairs to group numbers together with operations.

mcqs.q: Braces { } are also called what?
mcqs.why: The notes list the third kind of brackets, { }, as braces or curly brackets. The square brackets [ ] are the fourth kind, also called box brackets.

mcqs.q: Square brackets [ ] are also called what?
mcqs.why: The notes list the fourth kind of brackets, [ ], as square brackets or box brackets. Brackets are symbols used in pairs to group two or more numbers together with mathematical operations.

lessons.title: 3.5.2 Order of preferences as to remove the brackets from an expression
lessons.notes_html:
Order of preferences as to remove the brackets from an expression

If any mathematical problem involves more than one bracket, then brackets should be removed in the same order. Look at the example below: two students solve the same question in a different order. The expression is 30 × (40 − 24 + 10) + 7, where there is a bar (vinculum) over 24 + 10.

Step 1: Student-I (the right way) first solves the vinculum: 24 + 10, and because there is a '−' sign before it, it becomes −24 − 10 inside the brackets: 30 × (40 − 24 − 10) + 7.

Step 2: Then solve the parentheses: 30 × (40 − 34) + 7 = 30 × (6) + 7.

Step 3: Then multiply and add: 180 + 7 = 187.

Step 4: Student-II (the wrong way) removed the brackets without solving them first and got 30 × 40 − 34 + 7 = 1200 − 27 = 1173, which is wrong.

Final answer: The right way gives 187; brackets must be removed in order.

Preference of signs — always proceed from left to right

Step 1: (i) 3 + 8 − 4 = 11 − 4 = 7.

Step 2: (ii) 14 ÷ 2 × 5 = 7 × 5 = 35.

Final answer: Addition/subtraction and multiplication/division at the same level are done from left to right.

Rules for removing brackets

  • (ii) If there is a '+' sign before any pair of brackets, the brackets will be removed without changing the sign of the number within brackets. For example, 3 + (6 − 2) = 3 + (+4) = 3 + 4 = 7.
  • (iii) If there is a '−' sign before any pair of brackets, the brackets will be removed by changing the sign of the number within brackets. For example, 3 − (5 − 9) = 3 − (−4) = 3 + 4 = 7.
  • (iv) If there is no sign between a number (outside the pair of brackets) and a number within the brackets, then there will be multiplication between them, and brackets will be removed after multiplication. For example, 7(6 − 4) = 7(2) = 7 × 2 = 14.

The order of solving brackets

  • (i) "——" vinculum or bar is treated as first preference.
  • (ii) "( )" parentheses or curved brackets or round brackets are treated on second preference.
  • (iii) "{ }" curly brackets or braces are treated on third preference.
  • (iv) "[ ]" square brackets or box brackets are solved at the end.

mcqs.q: When an expression has more than one kind of bracket, which bracket is solved first?
mcqs.why: The order of solving brackets in the notes is: the vinculum or bar is treated as first preference, then parentheses, then braces, and square brackets are solved at the end.

mcqs.q: Parentheses ( ) are treated at which preference in removing brackets?
mcqs.why: The notes give the order: vinculum (bar) first, parentheses ( ) on second preference, braces { } on third preference, and square brackets [ ] solved at the end.

mcqs.q: Braces { } are treated at which preference in removing brackets?
mcqs.why: The notes give the order: vinculum (bar) first, parentheses ( ) second, braces { } on third preference, and square brackets [ ] solved at the end.

mcqs.q: Which brackets are solved at the end?
mcqs.why: The notes state that square brackets or box brackets [ ] are solved at the end, after the vinculum, the parentheses and the braces have all been removed in order.

mcqs.q: What is 30 x (40 - 24 + 10) + 7, where there is a bar (vinculum) over 24 + 10?
mcqs.why: Working: solve the vinculum first; the '-' sign before it makes it -24 - 10 inside: 30 x (40 - 24 - 10) + 7. Then the parentheses: 40 - 34 = 6, so 30 x 6 + 7. Then 180 + 7 = 187.

mcqs.q: What is 3 + 8 - 4, proceeding from left to right?
mcqs.why: Working: addition and subtraction are at the same level, so proceed from left to right: 3 + 8 = 11, then 11 - 4 = 7.

mcqs.q: What is 14 / 2 x 5, proceeding from left to right?
mcqs.why: Working: division and multiplication are at the same level, so proceed from left to right: 14 / 2 = 7, then 7 x 5 = 35.

mcqs.q: If there is a '+' sign before a pair of brackets, how are the brackets removed?
options: By changing the sign of the number within the brackets
Without changing the sign of the number within the brackets
By multiplying the number inside by the number outside
mcqs.why: The rule in the notes: with a '+' sign before the brackets, they are removed without changing the sign inside. Example: 3 + (6 - 2) = 3 + 4 = 7.

mcqs.q: What is 3 - (5 - 9)?
mcqs.why: Working: a '-' sign before the brackets changes the sign inside. First 5 - 9 = -4, so 3 - (-4) = 3 + 4 = 7.

mcqs.q: What is 7(6 - 4)?
mcqs.why: Working: there is no sign between 7 and the brackets, so there is multiplication between them. First 6 - 4 = 2, then 7 x 2 = 14.

lessons.title: 3.5.3 Recognize BODMAS Rule
lessons.notes_html:
Recognize BODMAS Rule

We have had an introductory discussion about the BODMAS rule in section 3.5.1. It shows the sequence where more than one operations are performed in the simplification of a mathematical expression. In some circumstances we call it as BIDMAS, BEDMAS, or PEDMAS, created to remember the order of operations. The letters of BODMAS are used for the order of fundamental operations:

BFor "Brackets"
OFor "of or order of operations"
DFor "Division"
MFor "Multiplication"
AFor "Addition"
SFor "Subtraction"

By using the BODMAS rule, we can simplify any given mathematical expression involving brackets and arithmetic operations. Now look at the following examples.

Book Example 22 — Solve

Solve: 2020 − 18[5 × {19 − 17 + (70 ÷ 10 + 5)}], where there is a vinculum (bar) over 70 ÷ 10.

Step 1: Solve the vinculum first: 70 ÷ 10 = 7, so we get 2020 − 18[5 × {19 − 17 + (7 + 5)}].

Step 2: Solve the parentheses: 7 + 5 = 12, so 2020 − 18[5 × {19 − 17 + 12}].

Step 3: Solve the curly brackets: 19 − 17 + 12 = 2 + 12 = 14, so 2020 − 18[5 × 14].

Step 4: Solve the square brackets: 5 × 14 = 70, so 2020 − 18[70].

Step 5: Multiply: 18 × 70 = 1260, so 2020 − 1260.

Final answer: 760.

Book Example 23 — Simplify

Simplify: 3 × 11 + 4 − 2 + (64 ÷ 8).

Step 1: First compute the expression within the brackets: 64 ÷ 8 = 8, so 3 × 11 + 4 − 2 + (8).

Step 2: Remove the brackets: 3 × 11 + 4 − 2 + 8.

Step 3: According to BODMAS, apply multiplication: 3 × 11 = 33, so 33 + 4 − 2 + 8.

Step 4: Now add or subtract from left to right: 33 + 4 = 37; 37 − 2 = 35; 35 + 8 = 43.

Final answer: 43.

Book Example 24 — Simplify

Simplify: 4 × 2 − [28 ÷ {3 + (8 + 6 − 3)}], where there is a bar (vinculum) over 6 − 3.

Step 1: First compute the bar or vinculum: 6 − 3 = 3.

Step 2: Compute the expression within the round brackets: (8 + 3) = 11, so 4 × 2 − [28 ÷ {3 + 11}].

Step 3: Compute the expression within the braces: {3 + 11} = 14, so 4 × 2 − [28 ÷ 14].

Step 4: Compute the expression within the square brackets: 28 ÷ 14 = 2, so 4 × 2 − 2.

Step 5: Multiply or divide from left to right: 4 × 2 = 8.

Step 6: Add or subtract from left to right: 8 − 2 = 6.

Final answer: 6.

Book Example 25 — Nabeel's diaries

Nabeel is a bookshop owner. He orders 30 new year diaries. The cost of each diary is Rs. 300. He paid Rs. 530 for shipping. How much did Nabeel spend in all?

Step 1: Total number of diaries = 30; cost of each diary = Rs. 300; shipping cost = Rs. 530.

Step 2: Total spending = (30 × 300) + 530.

Step 3: Multiply first (BODMAS): 30 × 300 = 9000.

Step 4: Add: 9000 + 530 = 9530.

Final answer: Nabeel spent Rs. 9530 in all.

Book Example 26 — Waseem's office items

Waseem purchased the following items for his office: four chairs at the rate of Rs. 950 each, three tables at the rate of Rs. 2500 each, and two desktop computers at the rate of Rs. 4500 each. How much money did Waseem spend altogether?

Step 1: Price of four chairs = 950 × 4 = Rs. 3800.

Step 2: Price of three computer tables = 2500 × 3 = Rs. 7500.

Step 3: Price of two desktop computers = 4500 × 2 = Rs. 9000.

Step 4: Total amount paid by Waseem = (950 × 4) + (2500 × 3) + (4500 × 2) = 3800 + 7500 + 9000 = 20,300.

Final answer: Waseem spent Rs. 20,300 altogether.

mcqs.q: In the BODMAS rule, what does the letter 'B' stand for?
mcqs.why: The notes expand BODMAS letter by letter: B stands for Brackets, O for 'of' or order of operations, D for Division, M for Multiplication, A for Addition and S for Subtraction.

mcqs.q: In the BODMAS rule, what does the letter 'O' stand for?
mcqs.why: The notes state that in BODMAS, O stands for 'of' or order of operations, coming after B for Brackets and before D for Division and M for Multiplication.

mcqs.q: In some circumstances, the BODMAS rule is also called what?
mcqs.why: The notes say that in some circumstances we call the same order of operations BIDMAS, BEDMAS or PEDMAS; all of them are memory aids for the same sequence of operations.
Working: brackets first: 64 / 8 = 8. Then multiplication: 3 x 11 = 33, giving 33 + 4 - 2 + 8. Then left to right: 33 + 4 = 37, 37 - 2 = 35, 35 + 8 = 43.
