mcqs.q: In 2020 - 18[5 x {19 - 17 + (70 / 10 + 5)}], with a vinculum over 70 / 10, what is solved first and what is its value?
mcqs.why: Working: the vinculum has first preference, so first solve 70 / 10 = 7. The expression becomes 2020 - 18[5 x {19 - 17 + (7 + 5)}], and only then are the other brackets solved in order.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 2020 - 18[5 x {19 - 17 + (70 / 10 + 5)}], with a vinculum over 70 / 10.
mcqs.why: Working: vinculum: 70 / 10 = 7. Parentheses: 7 + 5 = 12. Curly brackets: 19 - 17 + 12 = 14. Square brackets: 5 x 14 = 70. Multiply: 18 x 70 = 1260. Finally 2020 - 1260 = 760.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 4 x 2 - [28 / {3 + (8 + 6 - 3)}], where there is a bar (vinculum) over 6 - 3.
mcqs.why: Working: vinculum: 6 - 3 = 3. Round brackets: 8 + 3 = 11. Braces: 3 + 11 = 14. Square brackets: 28 / 14 = 2. Then 4 x 2 = 8, and 8 - 2 = 6.

mcqs.q: Nabeel orders 30 diaries at Rs. 300 each and pays Rs. 530 for shipping. How much did he spend in all?
mcqs.why: Working: total spending = (30 x 300) + 530. Multiply first by BODMAS: 30 x 300 = 9000. Then add the shipping: 9000 + 530 = Rs. 9530.

mcqs.q: Waseem bought 4 chairs at Rs. 950 each, 3 tables at Rs. 2500 each and 2 computers at Rs. 4500 each. How much did he spend altogether?
mcqs.why: Working: chairs 950 x 4 = 3800; tables 2500 x 3 = 7500; computers 4500 x 2 = 9000. Total = 3800 + 7500 + 9000 = Rs. 20,300.

mcqs.q: After the brackets in a BODMAS expression, in which order are the remaining operations done?
options: Addition, then subtraction, then multiplication, then division
Multiplication, then addition, then division, then subtraction
Division, then multiplication, then addition, then subtraction
Subtraction, then addition, then multiplication, then division
mcqs.why: BODMAS gives the sequence Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. So after brackets, division comes first, then multiplication, then addition, then subtraction (same-level operations from left to right).

lessons.title: 3.5.4 Simplify the mathematical expressions involving fractions and decimals groupes
lessons.notes_html:
Simplify the mathematical expressions involving fractions and decimals

The BODMAS rule can also be used to simplify the mathematical expressions involving decimals and fractions. Now look at the following examples.

Book Example 27 — Simplify

Simplify: 14.75 + [3.20 − {1.60 ÷ 2 × (12.50 + 13.90 − 5.90)}].

Step 1: Solve the parentheses first, from left to right: 12.50 + 13.90 − 5.90 = 26.40 − 5.90 = 20.50. The expression becomes 14.75 + [3.20 − {1.60 ÷ 2 × 20.50}].

Step 2: Inside the curly brackets, division and multiplication are done from left to right: 1.60 ÷ 2 = 0.80.

Step 3: 0.80 × 20.50 = 16.40. The expression becomes 14.75 + [3.20 − 16.40].

Step 4: Solve the square brackets: 3.20 − 16.40 = −13.20. The expression becomes 14.75 − 13.20.

Step 5: 14.75 − 13.20 = 1.55.

Final answer: 1.55.

Book Example 28 — Shabana's vegetables

One day Shabana went to Sunday bazar to buy vegetables with her mother. She bought 3 kg beetroot at Rs. 50 per kg, 1/4 kg garlic at Rs. 200 per kg, 2 1/2 kg okra at Rs. 60 per kg and 5 kg onion at Rs. 20 per kg. How much money did she spend to buy all the vegetables?

Step 1: Price of 3 kg beetroot = 3 × 50 = Rs. 150.

Step 2: Price of 1/4 kg garlic = 1/4 × 200 = Rs. 50.

Step 3: Price of 2 1/2 kg okra = 2 1/2 × 60 = 5/2 × 60 = Rs. 150.

Step 4: Price of 5 kg onion = 5 × 20 = Rs. 100.

Step 5: By using the BODMAS rule, total price of all the vegetables = (3 × 50) + (1/4 × 200) + (2 1/2 × 60) + (5 × 20) = 150 + 50 + 150 + 100 = 450.

Final answer: Shabana spent Rs. 450 to buy all the vegetables.

Worked examples — Exercise 3.3

Q1. Simplify the following:

(i) 4 + 6 − 7 × 15 ÷ 3

Step 1: By BODMAS, do division and multiplication before addition and subtraction. First, 15 ÷ 3 = 5.

Step 2: Then multiply: 7 × 5 = 35. The expression becomes 4 + 6 − 35.

Step 3: Add and subtract from left to right: 4 + 6 = 10; 10 − 35 = −25.

Final answer: −25.

(ii) 25 + (8 × 24 ÷ 2 − 26)

Step 1: Solve the brackets first. Inside, do multiplication and division from left to right: 8 × 24 = 192.

Step 2: 192 ÷ 2 = 96.

Step 3: 96 − 26 = 70. The expression becomes 25 + 70.

Step 4: 25 + 70 = 95.

Final answer: 95.

(iii) 44 − {26 + (−84 × 84 ÷ 42)}

Step 1: Solve the round brackets first: inside, 84 ÷ 42 = 2.

Step 2: −84 × 2 = −168. The expression becomes 44 − {26 + (−168)}.

Step 3: Solve the curly brackets: 26 + (−168) = −142. The expression becomes 44 − (−142).

Step 4: A '−' sign before the brackets changes the sign inside: 44 + 142 = 186.

Final answer: 186.

(iv) 86 ÷ (37 + {29 − (114 ÷ 6 + 9 − 5)}]

Step 1: Solve the round brackets first, from left to right: 114 ÷ 6 = 19; 19 + 9 − 5 = 23.

Step 2: Solve the curly brackets: 29 − 23 = 6.

Step 3: Solve the outer brackets: 37 + 6 = 43. The expression becomes 86 ÷ 43.

Step 4: 86 ÷ 43 = 2.

Final answer: 2.

(v) 230 × [184 − {276 ÷ 138 × 124 ÷ 4 − 30}] (the book prints a vinculum bar over 4 − 30)

Step 1: Solve the curly brackets first. Inside, do division and multiplication from left to right: 276 ÷ 138 = 2.

Step 2: 2 × 124 = 248.

Step 3: 248 ÷ 4 = 62.

Step 4: 62 − 30 = 32, so the curly brackets give 32.

Step 5: Solve the square brackets: 184 − 32 = 152.

Step 6: Multiply: 230 × 152 = 34,960.

Final answer: 34,960. (Note: the book's Answers section lists 41,860 for this question; the value above follows the standard BODMAS order for the expression in figures.)

(vi) 221 + [616 − {347 + (435 ÷ 3 × 2 − 36 − 6)}], where there is a vinculum (bar) over 36 − 6

Step 1: Solve the vinculum first: 36 − 6 = 30.

Step 2: Solve the round brackets: inside, 435 ÷ 3 = 145; 145 × 2 = 290; 290 − 30 = 260.

Step 3: Solve the curly brackets: 347 + 260 = 607.

Step 4: Solve the square brackets: 616 − 607 = 9.

Step 5: 221 + 9 = 230.

Final answer: 230.

Q2. Use the order of operations to simplify the following:

(i) 19.5 + 12.8 − 13.5

Step 1: Add and subtract from left to right: 19.5 + 12.8 = 32.3.

Step 2: 32.3 − 13.5 = 18.8.

Final answer: 18.8.

(ii) 8.8 ÷ 2.2 − (−2.8)

Step 1: Do the division first: 8.8 ÷ 2.2 = 4.

Step 2: Subtracting a negative changes its sign: 4 − (−2.8) = 4 + 2.8 = 6.8.

Final answer: 6.8.

(iii) 30.8 ÷ (3.1 + 0.4)

Step 1: Solve the brackets first: 3.1 + 0.4 = 3.5.

Step 2: Divide: 30.8 ÷ 3.5 = 8.8.

Final answer: 8.8.

(iv) 16.31 + {2.50 − (5.94 ÷ 2.20 × 4.0 − 18.75)}

Step 1: Solve the round brackets: inside, do division and multiplication from left to right: 5.94 ÷ 2.20 = 2.7.

Step 2: 2.7 × 4.0 = 10.8.

Step 3: 10.8 − 18.75 = −7.95.

Step 4: Solve the curly brackets: 2.50 − (−7.95) = 2.50 + 7.95 = 10.45.

Step 5: 16.31 + 10.45 = 26.76.

Final answer: 26.76.

(v) 433.29 − [505.25 + {113.18 ÷ (89.5 + 24.97 − 1.29)}]

Step 1: Solve the round brackets from left to right: 89.5 + 24.97 = 114.47; 114.47 − 1.29 = 113.18.

Step 2: Solve the curly brackets: 113.18 ÷ 113.18 = 1.

Step 3: Solve the square brackets: 505.25 + 1 = 506.25.

Step 4: 433.29 − 506.25 = −72.96.

Final answer: −72.96.

(vi) 5.50 − [6.10 × 2 − {39 + (4.5 + 8 − 2)}], where there is a vinculum (bar) over 8 − 2

Step 1: Solve the vinculum first: 8 − 2 = 6.

Step 2: Solve the round brackets: 4.5 + 6 = 10.5.

Step 3: Solve the curly brackets: 39 + 10.5 = 49.5.

Step 4: Solve the multiplication inside the square brackets: 6.10 × 2 = 12.20.

Step 5: Solve the square brackets: 12.20 − 49.5 = −37.3.

Step 6: 5.50 − (−37.3) = 5.50 + 37.3 = 42.8.

Final answer: 42.8.

(vii) 5.2 + [0.5 − {6.4 + (−9 + 5 − 3)}]

Step 1: Solve the round brackets from left to right: −9 + 5 − 3 = −4 − 3 = −7.

Step 2: Solve the curly brackets: 6.4 + (−7) = −0.6.

Step 3: Solve the square brackets: 0.5 − (−0.6) = 0.5 + 0.6 = 1.1.

Step 4: 5.2 + 1.1 = 6.3.

Final answer: 6.3.

Q3. Simplify the following by using the order of operations:

(i) 3 4/99 + 4 7/33 − 5 9/11

Step 1: Make the denominators equal. The LCM of 99, 33 and 11 is 99: 4 7/33 = 4 21/99 and 5 9/11 = 5 81/99.

Step 2: Add the first two: 3 4/99 + 4 21/99 = 7 25/99.

Step 3: Subtract: 7 25/99 − 5 81/99 = 6 124/99 − 5 81/99 = 1 43/99.

Final answer: 1 43/99.

(ii) 4 8/9 × 3 5/14 ÷ 1 1/14

Step 1: Change the mixed fractions into improper fractions: 4 8/9 = 40/9, 3 5/14 = 47/14 and 1 1/14 = 15/14.

Step 2: Change the division into multiplication by the reciprocal: 40/9 × 47/14 × 14/15.

Step 3: Cancel 14 with 14: 40 × 47 / (9 × 15) = 1880/135.

Step 4: Simplify: 1880/135 = 376/27 = 13 25/27.

Final answer: 13 25/27.

(iii) 7/18 + (5/9 ÷ 1/3)

Step 1: Solve the brackets first: 5/9 ÷ 1/3 = 5/9 × 3/1 = 15/9 = 5/3.

Step 2: Add: 7/18 + 5/3. The LCM of 18 and 3 is 18, and 5/3 = 30/18.

Step 3: 7/18 + 30/18 = 37/18 = 2 1/18.

Final answer: 2 1/18.

(iv) 5/9 + (7/18 + 1/3 − 1/6 + 1/2)

Step 1: Solve the brackets first. The LCM of 18, 3, 6 and 2 is 18: 7/18 + 6/18 − 3/18 + 9/18 = 19/18.

Step 2: Add: 5/9 + 19/18. As 5/9 = 10/18, we get 10/18 + 19/18 = 29/18.

Step 3: 29/18 = 1 11/18.

Final answer: 1 11/18.

(v) 8/33 × (9/11 ÷ 3/22)

Step 1: Solve the brackets first: 9/11 ÷ 3/22 = 9/11 × 22/3 = 6.

Step 2: Multiply: 8/33 × 6 = 48/33.

Step 3: Simplify: 48/33 = 16/11 = 1 5/11.

Final answer: 1 5/11.

(vi) 5/12 + {11/24 − (2/3 + 7/8 − 2/3)}, where there is a vinculum (bar) over 7/8 − 2/3

Step 1: Solve the vinculum first: 7/8 − 2/3 = 21/24 − 16/24 = 5/24.

Step 2: Solve the round brackets: 2/3 + 5/24 = 16/24 + 5/24 = 21/24 = 7/8.

Step 3: Solve the curly brackets: 11/24 − 7/8 = 11/24 − 21/24 = −10/24 = −5/12.

Step 4: Add: 5/12 + (−5/12) = 0.

Final answer: 0.

(vii) −3 9/24 ÷ [4 3/8 × {1/2 + (5 1/2 − 6 1/2)}]

Step 1: Solve the round brackets: 5 1/2 − 6 1/2 = −1.

Step 2: Solve the curly brackets: 1/2 + (−1) = −1/2.

Step 3: Solve the square brackets: 4 3/8 = 35/8, and 35/8 × (−1/2) = −35/16.

Step 4: Change −3 9/24 into an improper fraction: −3 9/24 = −27/8. Divide: (−27/8) ÷ (−35/16) = 27/8 × 16/35.

Step 5: 27 × 16 / (8 × 35) = 54/35 = 1 19/35 (like signs give a positive result).

Final answer: 1 19/35.

(viii) 1 5/7 of 21 + 3 3/4 ÷ 3/7 − 1 1/3

Step 1: By BODMAS, 'of' means multiplication and is done first: 1 5/7 of 21 = 12/7 × 21 = 36.

Step 2: Do the division next: 3 3/4 ÷ 3/7 = 15/4 × 7/3 = 35/4.

Step 3: The expression becomes 36 + 35/4 − 1 1/3. With the common denominator 12: 432/12 + 105/12 − 16/12 = 521/12.

Step 4: 521/12 = 43 5/12.

Final answer: 43 5/12.

Q4. There are 320 students in a school. 220 students receive pocket money Rs. 50 per day and the rest receive Rs. 70 per day. To the management of school, a week is equal to six working days. How much amount do all the students spend in a week?

Step 1: Students receiving Rs. 70 per day = 320 − 220 = 100.

Step 2: Amount per day for the first group = 220 × 50 = Rs. 11,000.

Step 3: Amount per day for the rest = 100 × 70 = Rs. 7,000.

Step 4: Total amount per day = 11,000 + 7,000 = Rs. 18,000.

Step 5: A week has six working days, so the amount in a week = 18,000 × 6 = Rs. 108,000.

Final answer: All the students spend Rs. 108,000 in a week.

Q5. A factory worker makes 90 bars of soap in a week and sells these at the rate of Rs. 250 each. Before the soap can all be sold, the workers found out 10 bars were nibbled by mice. How much will be the total sale at the end of a four week month?

Step 1: Bars made in four weeks = 90 × 4 = 360 bars.

Step 2: Saleable bars = 360 − 10 = 350 bars.

Step 3: Total sale = 350 × 250 = Rs. 87,500.

Final answer: The total sale at the end of a four week month will be Rs. 87,500.

Q6. Shazmeena had 30.50 metres of cloth. She used 12.60 metres of cloth for her suit. She gives 10.80 metres of cloth to her friend. How much cloth is left with Shazmeena?

Step 1: Total cloth used and given = 12.60 + 10.80 = 23.40 metres.

Step 2: Cloth left = 30.50 − 23.40 = 7.10 metres.

Final answer: 7.10 metres of cloth is left with Shazmeena.

Q7. The price of 20 kg chemical is Rs. 25000. Find the price of 13 kg chemical.

Step 1: Price of 1 kg chemical = 25000 ÷ 20 = Rs. 1250.

Step 2: Price of 13 kg chemical = 1250 × 13 = Rs. 16,250.

Final answer: The price of 13 kg chemical is Rs. 16,250.

Q8. Nasreen bought 15 metres of cloth from the market. She used half of the cloth for her suit, 1/3 part of it for her little daughter. She used the remaining cloth for her niece's suit. How much cloth did she use for her niece's suit?

Step 1: Cloth for her own suit = half of 15 = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5 metres.

Step 2: Cloth for her daughter = 1/3 of 15 = 5 metres.

Step 3: Cloth used in all = 7.5 + 5 = 12.5 metres.

Step 4: Remaining cloth for her niece's suit = 15 − 12.5 = 2.5 metres.

Final answer: She used 2.5 metres of cloth for her niece's suit.

Q9. Sakeena required 24 1/4 metres long wire for a connection. She joined three lengths of wires 4 3/4 metres, 5 1/8 metres and 6 1/2 metres. How much more length of wire did she need?

Step 1: Add the joined lengths. The LCM of 4, 8 and 2 is 8: 4 3/4 = 4 6/8, 5 1/8 = 5 1/8 and 6 1/2 = 6 4/8.

Step 2: 4 6/8 + 5 1/8 + 6 4/8 = 15 11/8 = 16 3/8 metres.

Step 3: Wire still needed = 24 1/4 − 16 3/8 = 24 2/8 − 16 3/8.

Step 4: Borrow 1 from 24: 23 10/8 − 16 3/8 = 7 7/8 metres.

Final answer: She needed 7 7/8 metres more length of wire.

Summary of Sub-Domain 3

  • The integers with the same signs are called like integers; the integers with different signs are called unlike integers.
  • According to the commutative law of addition, the sum of two integers remains unchanged by changing the "order".
  • Zero (0) is an integer, neither positive nor negative.
  • According to the associative law of addition, changing the "grouping" of addends does not change the sum.
  • According to the commutative law of multiplication, the product of two integers remains unchanged by changing their "order".
  • According to the associative law of multiplication, "changing grouping" of the factors does not change the product.
  • According to the distributive law of multiplication, multiplying an integer by the group of integers added together is same as doing each multiplication separately.
  • The product of two unlike integers is always negative.
  • The product of two like integers with negative signs is always positive.
  • Division of an integer by zero (0) is not possible.
  • The word BODMAS indicates the sequence in which more than one operations are performed in the simplification of mathematical expressions.
  • If there is a plus '+' sign before any pair of brackets, the brackets will be removed without changing the sign of the numbers within brackets.
  • If there is a minus '−' sign before any pair of brackets, the brackets will be removed with changing the sign of the number within brackets.
  • If there is no sign between a number (outside the pair of brackets) and a number within the brackets, then there will be multiplication between both numbers, and brackets will be removed after multiplication.
  • Brackets are solved in the following order: 1st vinculum or bar, 2nd ( ) parentheses, 3rd { } braces and 4th [ ] square brackets.

mcqs.why: Working: parentheses first: 12.50 + 13.90 - 5.90 = 20.50. Inside the braces, left to right: 1.60 / 2 = 0.80, then 0.80 x 20.50 = 16.40. Square brackets: 3.20 - 16.40 = -13.20. Finally 14.75 - 13.20 = 1.55.

mcqs.q: Shabana bought 3 kg beetroot at Rs. 50 per kg, 1/4 kg garlic at Rs. 200 per kg, 2 1/2 kg okra at Rs. 60 per kg and 5 kg onion at Rs. 20 per kg. How much did she spend in all?
mcqs.why: Working: beetroot 3 x 50 = 150; garlic 1/4 x 200 = 50; okra 2 1/2 x 60 = 150; onion 5 x 20 = 100. Total by BODMAS: 150 + 50 + 150 + 100 = Rs. 450.

mcqs.q: What is the price of 1/4 kg of garlic at Rs. 200 per kg?
mcqs.why: Working: price = 1/4 x 200. Divide 200 by 4: 200 / 4 = 50, so 1/4 kg of garlic costs Rs. 50, as in Shabana's shopping example.

mcqs.q: What is the price of 2 1/2 kg of okra at Rs. 60 per kg?
mcqs.why: Working: price = 2 1/2 x 60 = 5/2 x 60. First 60 / 2 = 30, then 5 x 30 = 150, so 2 1/2 kg of okra costs Rs. 150.
Working: addition and subtraction are done from left to right. Step 1: 19.5 + 12.8 = 32.3. Step 2: 32.3 - 13.5 = 18.8.
Working: division first: 8.8 / 2.2 = 4. Then subtracting a negative changes its sign: 4 - (-2.8) = 4 + 2.8 = 6.8.
Working: brackets first: 3.1 + 0.4 = 3.5. Then divide: 30.8 / 3.5 = 8.8, because 3.5 x 8.8 = 30.8.
Working: brackets first: 9/11 / 3/22 = 9/11 x 22/3 = 6. Then multiply: 8/33 x 6 = 48/33. Simplify: 48/33 = 16/11 = 1 5/11.

mcqs.q: Shazmeena had 30.50 metres of cloth. She used 12.60 metres for her suit and gave 10.80 metres to her friend. How much cloth is left?
mcqs.why: Working: cloth used and given = 12.60 + 10.80 = 23.40 metres. Cloth left = 30.50 - 23.40 = 7.10 metres.

chapters.title: Unit 4: Numbers and Operations — Sub-Domain 4: Rate, Ratio and Percentage

lessons.title: 4.1 RATIO
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Ratio?

Ratio: “The ratio is a numerical comparison between two quantities or things of same kind.” In daily life we use the word ratio while distributing quantities, money and other things. For example, there are four green mangoes to five yellow mangoes, written as 4 : 5.

Always compare the quantities of same kind with same unit, because the ratio of two same quantities can be defined, but the ratio of two different quantities is meaningless. For example, we cannot compare weight with height.

Three Forms of a Ratio

A ratio can be expressed in three forms: (i) Word form, (ii) Ratio form, (iii) Fraction form. The mango example shows all three forms:

  • 4 to 5 — in word form
  • 4 : 5 — in ratio form
  • 4/5 — in fraction form

Each form is read as “the ratio of 4 to 5”. In general we use ‘x’ for the first quantity and ‘y’ for the second quantity and write them as x : y, read as “the ratio of x to y”. If more than two quantities are given, we write them as x : y : z in the form of ratio.

4.1.1 Defining a Ratio

Every country of the world has its national flag. A national flag is a flag that represents and symbolizes a country. Pakistan’s National flag is in the ratio of height to length, which is 2 : 3. So for every 2 (centimetre, metre or feet) of height there must be 3 of length.

Example 1: If we make a flag of 20 cm high, it must be 30 cm long. If we make another flag of 40 cm high, it must be 60 cm long. Both times the flag is still in the ratio 2 : 3, so we can say: “The ratio is a relation in which one quantity bears to another quantity of the same kind with regards to their magnitude.”

4.1.2 Antecedent and Consequent in a Ratio

In the ratio of green to yellow mangoes, 4 : 5, the number 4 is the first element and the number 5 is the second element. “The first element is called antecedent and the second element is called consequent.”

  • Order of ratios always matters, i.e. 4 : 5 is not same as 5 : 4.
  • Ratio is unit less, or it has no unit.

Example 2: Write down the antecedent and consequent of the ratios: (i) 7 : 9 — Antecedent = 7, Consequent = 9. (ii) a : b — Antecedent = a, Consequent = b. (iii) 19 : 20 — Antecedent = 19, Consequent = 20.

4.1.3 Calculation of Ratio

Ratios are the mathematical expressions in which we compare two or more quantities. Ratios can be calculated and written in several different ways.

Example 3: Nimra used 8 table spoons milk and 24 table spoons unsalted butter to make her birthday cake. Write the ratio of milk to unsalted butter.

Step 1: Milk used = 8 table spoons; unsalted butter used = 24 table spoons.

Step 2: Ratio of milk to unsalted butter = 8 : 24, and dividing both terms by 8 gives 1 : 3.

Final answer: 8 : 24 = 1 : 3

Example 4: There are 400 students and 40 teachers in a school. Write the ratio of teachers to students.

Step 1: Number of teachers = 40; number of students = 400.

Step 2: Ratio of teachers to students = 40 : 400, and dividing both terms by 40 gives 1 : 10.

Final answer: 40 : 400 = 1 : 10

4.1.4 Simplification of Given Ratio into Lowest (Equivalent) Form

A ratio is another form of common fraction. To reduce the given ratios into the lowest (equivalent) form we divide each term of ratio by the H.C.F (Highest Common Factor) of all the terms. A ratio remains unchanged when both the terms are multiplied or divided by the same number. This is known as equivalent ratio.

Example 5: Reduce the following ratios into the lowest equivalent ratios. (i) 7 : 56

Step 1: H.C.F of 7 and 56 is 7.

Step 2: Divide each term of the ratio by 7: 7/7 : 56/7.

Final answer: 1 : 8

Example 5 (ii): 9 : 36 : 48

Step 1: HCF of 9, 36 and 48 is 3.

Step 2: Divide each term by 3: 9/3 : 36/3 : 48/3.

Final answer: 3 : 12 : 16

Example 6: There are 40 boys and 60 girls in two sections of Mathematics class. Find the ratio of boys to girls in both sections, and write the answer in the simplest form.

Step 1: Number of boys = 40; number of girls = 60, so boys : girls = 40 : 60.

Step 2: H.C.F of 40 and 60 is 20.

Step 3: Divide each term of ratio by 20: 40/20 : 60/20 = 2 : 3.

Final answer: The ratio of boys to girls is 2 : 3

Worked examples — Practice-1

Practice-1 Q1(i): Simplify the ratio 60 : 2000.

Step 1: Find the H.C.F of 60 and 2000, which is 20.

Step 2: Divide each term by 20: 60 ÷ 20 : 2000 ÷ 20 = 3 : 100.

Final answer: 3 : 100

Practice-1 Q1(ii): Simplify the ratio 25 : 625.

Step 1: Find the H.C.F of 25 and 625, which is 25.

Step 2: Divide each term by 25: 25 ÷ 25 : 625 ÷ 25 = 1 : 25.

Final answer: 1 : 25

Practice-1 Q2: Rehman earns Rs. 500 in an hour and spends Rs. 350. Find the ratio of his income to expenditure.

Step 1: Write the ratio income : expenditure = 500 : 350.

Step 2: H.C.F of 500 and 350 is 50.

Step 3: Divide each term by 50: 500 ÷ 50 : 350 ÷ 50 = 10 : 7.

Final answer: 10 : 7

4.1.5 Relationship Between Ratio and Fraction

The ratio can also be expressed in fraction form, where the numerator is called antecedent and the denominator is called consequent. For example, 3 : 5 = 3/5. Similarly, in general a : b = a/b, where ‘a’ is antecedent and ‘b’ is consequent. A ratio has no unit. It is just a number which indicates how many times one quantity is greater than the other.

Example 7: First write in fraction form and then simplify. (i) 18 : 24 = 18/24 = 3/4, hence 18 : 24 = 3 : 4. (ii) 40 : 70 = 40/70 = 4/7, hence 40 : 70 = 4 : 7. (iii) 25 : 45 = 25/45 = 5/9, hence 25 : 45 = 5 : 9.

Worked examples — Practice-2

Practice-2 (i): Write the ratio 7 : 11 in the form of fraction and simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 7 : 11 = 7/11.

Step 2: 7 and 11 have no common factor except 1, so the fraction cannot be simplified further.

Final answer: 7/11, i.e. 7 : 11

Practice-2 (ii): Write the ratio 14 : 29 in the form of fraction and simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 14 : 29 = 14/29.

Step 2: 14 and 29 have no common factor except 1, so the fraction cannot be simplified further.

Final answer: 14/29, i.e. 14 : 29

Example 8(i): Find the ratio of 5/6 and 2/9 and write in the simplest form.

Step 1: Write as a ratio: 5/6 : 2/9.

Step 2: Multiply both by the LCM of 6 and 9, which is 18: 5/6 × 18 : 2/9 × 18.

Step 3: 5 × 3 : 2 × 2 = 15 : 4.

Final answer: 15 : 4

Example 8(ii): Find the ratio of 1 5/6 km, 1 11/15 km and 1 13/30 km and write in the simplest form.

Step 1: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions: 1 5/6 km : 1 11/15 km : 1 13/30 km = 11/5 km : 26/15 km : 43/30 km.

Step 2: Multiply all by the LCM of 5, 15 and 30, which is 30: 11/5 × 30 : 26/15 × 30 : 43/30 × 30.

Step 3: 66 : 52 : 43, which has no common factor for all terms.

Final answer: 66 : 52 : 43

Example 9: Naseem has Rs. 1600. She shared this amount with her two friends Rabia and Fatima in the ratio 3 : 5. How much amount did each of them receive from Naseem?

Step 1: Total amount with Naseem = Rs. 1600. The sum of money is divided into 3 + 5 = 8 equal parts. Rabia and Fatima received 3 and 5 parts respectively.

Step 2: Rabia received = 3/8 of 1600 = 3/8 × 1600 = 3 × 200 = Rs. 600.

Step 3: Fatima received = 5/8 of 1600 = 5/8 × 1600 = 5 × 200 = Rs. 1000.

Step 4: Check: Rabia + Fatima = 600 + 1000 = 1600. ✓

Final answer: Rabia received Rs. 600 and Fatima received Rs. 1000

Worked examples — Practice-3

Practice-3 (i): Find the ratio of 500 g to 1 kg.

Step 1: Convert both quantities to the same unit: 1 kg = 1000 g.

Step 2: Write the ratio: 500 g : 1000 g = 500 : 1000.

Step 3: Divide each term by the H.C.F 500: 1 : 2.

Final answer: 1 : 2

Practice-3 (ii): Find the ratio of 3/5 to 7/9.

Step 1: Write as a ratio: 3/5 : 7/9.

Step 2: Multiply both by the LCM of 5 and 9, which is 45: 3/5 × 45 : 7/9 × 45.

Step 3: 3 × 9 : 7 × 5 = 27 : 35.

Final answer: 27 : 35

4.1.6 Continued Ratio

If ‘a’ and ‘b’ are two quantities having same units where b ≠ 0, then the ratio of a and b can be written as a : b, read as “a ratio b”. Sometimes we compare more than two quantities. “The comparison among three or more quantities is called continued ratio.” If a, b, c, d, e and f are in continued ratio, then a : b = b : c = c : d = d : e = e : f. In fraction form: a/b = b/c = c/d = d/e = e/f. Always compare the same quantities with same units.

Continued ratio is used in daily life, for example: (i) ratio among the shares of profit between three or more persons; (ii) ratio among the prices of three or more different types of cars, etc.

Example 10: Nadia wants to distribute Rs. 9435 among her three children Nida, Rehan and Aleem. She distributed this money in such a way that Nida : Rehan = 4 : 5 and Rehan : Aleem = 3 : 2. How much money will each child get?

Step 1: Total amount with Nadia = Rs. 9435. Make the common quantity (Rehan) the same in both ratios: Nida : Rehan : Aleem = 4 × 3 : 3 × 5 : 5 × 2 = 12 : 15 : 10.

Step 2: Sum of ratios = 12 + 15 + 10 = 37.

Step 3: Nida’s share = 12/37 × 9435 = Rs. 3060.

Step 4: Rehan’s share = 15/37 × 9435 = Rs. 3825.

Step 5: Aleem’s share = 10/37 × 9435 = Rs. 2550.

Step 6: Check: 3060 + 3825 + 2550 = Rs. 9435. ✓

Final answer: Nida Rs. 3060, Rehan Rs. 3825, Aleem Rs. 2550

To solve any type of word problem follow four steps: (i) Read: read the statement of the given problem until you understand. (ii) Plan: after understanding, plan to find the required things and decide which method to apply. (iii) Solve: make a calculation and find the required thing from the given facts. (iv) Check: finally check your solution by applying different methods or revise your solution.

Worked examples — Practice (Continued Ratio)

The total price of three electronic items is in the ratio: washing machine to fridge is 2 : 3 and fridge to AC is 4 : 5. If Saba paid Rs. 98000, then find the price of each item.

Step 1: Make the common quantity (fridge) the same: multiply the first ratio by 4 and the second ratio by 3. Washing machine : Fridge : AC = 8 : 12 : 15.

Step 2: Sum of ratios = 8 + 12 + 15 = 35. One part = 98000 ÷ 35 = Rs. 2800.

Step 3: Washing machine = 8 × 2800 = Rs. 22400. Fridge = 12 × 2800 = Rs. 33600. AC = 15 × 2800 = Rs. 42000.

Step 4: Check: 22400 + 33600 + 42000 = 98000. ✓

Final answer: Washing machine Rs. 22400, Fridge Rs. 33600, AC Rs. 42000

Worked examples — Exercise 4.1

The table shows the obtained marks of grade-6 students in a Mathematics test: Shoukat 55, Saima 62, Waseem 46, Ali 85, Rabia 70, Hiba 35, Arslan 50, Zeeshan 80.

Name of pupilMarks
Shoukat55
Saima62
Waseem46
Ali85
Rabia70
Hiba35
Arslan50
Zeeshan80

Q1(i): Write the ratio of obtained marks of Zeeshan to Arslan in the other two forms.

Step 1: Read the marks from the table: Zeeshan = 80, Arslan = 50. The given form is word form: Zeeshan to Arslan.

Step 2: Ratio form: 80 : 50.

Step 3: Fraction form: 80/50.

Final answer: Ratio form 80 : 50; Fraction form 80/50

Q1(ii): Write the ratio of obtained marks of Hiba to Shoukat in the other two forms.

Step 1: Read the marks: Hiba = 35, Shoukat = 55.

Step 2: Ratio form: 35 : 55.

Step 3: Fraction form: 35/55.

Final answer: Ratio form 35 : 55; Fraction form 35/55

Q1(iii): Write the ratio of obtained marks of Waseem to Rabia in the other two forms.

Step 1: Read the marks: Waseem = 46, Rabia = 70.

Step 2: Ratio form: 46 : 70.

Step 3: Fraction form: 46/70.

Final answer: Ratio form 46 : 70; Fraction form 46/70

Q1(iv): Write the ratio of obtained marks of Ali to Arslan in the other two forms.

Step 1: Read the marks: Ali = 85, Arslan = 50.

Step 2: Ratio form: 85 : 50.

Step 3: Fraction form: 85/50.

Final answer: Ratio form 85 : 50; Fraction form 85/50

Q1(v): Write the ratio of obtained marks of Shoukat to Ali in the other two forms.

Step 1: Read the marks: Shoukat = 55, Ali = 85.

Step 2: Ratio form: 55 : 85.

Step 3: Fraction form: 55/85.

Final answer: Ratio form 55 : 85; Fraction form 55/85

Q1(vi): Write the ratio of obtained marks of Shoukat to Ali to Arslan in the other form.

Step 1: Read the marks: Shoukat = 55, Ali = 85, Arslan = 50.

Step 2: Ratio form for three quantities: 55 : 85 : 50.

Final answer: 55 : 85 : 50

Q1(vii): Write the ratio of obtained marks of Waseem to Saima to Rabia in the other form.

Step 1: Read the marks: Waseem = 46, Saima = 62, Rabia = 70.

Step 2: Ratio form for three quantities: 46 : 62 : 70.

Final answer: 46 : 62 : 70

Q2: Write each of the following into ratio form: (i) 3/5 (ii) 7/12 (iii) 34/37 (iv) 53/59 (v) 101/103 (vi) x/y (vii) x/(x + 1) (viii) (a − b)/(p + q).

Step 1: In fraction form the numerator is the antecedent and the denominator is the consequent, so a/b is written as a : b.

Step 2: Apply this to each fraction one by one.

Final answer: (i) 3 : 5 (ii) 7 : 12 (iii) 34 : 37 (iv) 53 : 59 (v) 101 : 103 (vi) x : y (vii) x : (x + 1) (viii) (a − b) : (p + q)

Q3(i): Express the ratio 50 : 60 into fraction form and then simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 50 : 60 = 50/60.

Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 10: 50/60 = 5/6.

Final answer: 5/6, i.e. 5 : 6

Q3(ii): Express the ratio 55 : 65 into fraction form and then simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 55 : 65 = 55/65.

Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 5: 55/65 = 11/13.

Final answer: 11/13, i.e. 11 : 13

Q3(iii): Express the ratio 30 : 60 into fraction form and then simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 30 : 60 = 30/60.

Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 30: 30/60 = 1/2.

Final answer: 1/2, i.e. 1 : 2

Q3(iv): Express the ratio 85 : 90 into fraction form and then simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 85 : 90 = 85/90.

Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 5: 85/90 = 17/18.

Final answer: 17/18, i.e. 17 : 18

Q3(v): Express the ratio 75 : 85 into fraction form and then simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 75 : 85 = 75/85.

Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 5: 75/85 = 15/17.

Final answer: 15/17, i.e. 15 : 17

Q3(vi): Express the ratio 85 : 95 into fraction form and then simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 85 : 95 = 85/95.

Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 5: 85/95 = 17/19.

Final answer: 17/19, i.e. 17 : 19

Q3(vii): Express the ratio 56 : 70 into fraction form and then simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 56 : 70 = 56/70.

Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 14: 56/70 = 4/5.

Final answer: 4/5, i.e. 4 : 5

Q3(viii): Express the ratio 0.6 : 0.9 into fraction form and then simplify.

Step 1: Write in fraction form: 0.6 : 0.9 = 0.6/0.9.

Step 2: Multiply numerator and denominator by 10 to remove the decimals: 6/9.

Step 3: Divide numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 3: 6/9 = 2/3.

Final answer: 2/3, i.e. 2 : 3

Q4: During a PSL (Pakistan Super League) match Naveed completed his century in one hour while Sarfraz took 1 hour 30 minutes. What is the ratio of time taken by both the players to reach their centuries? Write the ratio in the simplest form.

Step 1: Convert both times to the same unit, minutes: Naveed = 1 hour = 60 minutes; Sarfraz = 1 hour 30 minutes = 90 minutes.

Step 2: Write the ratio: 60 : 90.

Step 3: Divide each term by the H.C.F 30: 60 ÷ 30 : 90 ÷ 30 = 2 : 3.

Final answer: 2 : 3

Q5: Aneel’s monthly salary is Rs. 55,000. He spends his monthly salary in the ratio 2 : 3 as saving and expenditure respectively. Find his monthly expenditure and saving.

Step 1: Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 = 5.

Step 2: Saving = 2/5 of 55000 = 2/5 × 55000 = Rs. 22,000.

Step 3: Expenditure = 3/5 of 55000 = 3/5 × 55000 = Rs. 33,000.

Step 4: Check: 22,000 + 33,000 = 55,000. ✓

Final answer: Saving Rs. 22,000; Expenditure Rs. 33,000

Q6: Distribute Rs. 99,000 among three brothers Moeez, Zurain and Abdul Hadi, such that Moeez : Zurain = 4 : 5 and Zurain : Abdul Hadi = 5 : 6.

Step 1: The common quantity Zurain is already 5 in both ratios, so the continued ratio is Moeez : Zurain : Abdul Hadi = 4 : 5 : 6.

Step 2: Sum of ratios = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15. One part = 99,000 ÷ 15 = Rs. 6,600.

Step 3: Moeez = 4 × 6,600 = Rs. 26,400. Zurain = 5 × 6,600 = Rs. 33,000. Abdul Hadi = 6 × 6,600 = Rs. 39,600.

Step 4: Check: 26,400 + 33,000 + 39,600 = 99,000. ✓

Final answer: Moeez Rs. 26,400, Zurain Rs. 33,000, Abdul Hadi Rs. 39,600

mcqs.q: What is a ratio?
options: A comparison of weight with height
A numerical comparison between two quantities of the same kind
A comparison with different units only
mcqs.why: The notes define ratio as a numerical comparison between two quantities or things of the same kind, for example 4 green mangoes to 5 yellow mangoes is 4 : 5.

mcqs.q: Pakistan's flag is in the ratio height : length = 2 : 3. If a flag is 20 cm high, how long must it be?
mcqs.why: Working: height : length = 2 : 3, so length = 20 / 2 x 3 = 10 x 3 = 30 cm, keeping the same ratio 2 : 3.

mcqs.q: In the ratio 7 : 9, what is the antecedent?
mcqs.why: In a ratio the first element is called the antecedent and the second is the consequent, so in 7 : 9 the antecedent is 7 and the consequent is 9.

mcqs.q: Nimra used 8 tablespoons of milk and 24 tablespoons of unsalted butter. What is the ratio of milk to butter in simplest form?
mcqs.why: Working: milk : butter = 8 : 24. Dividing both terms by 8 gives 8/8 : 24/8 = 1 : 3.

mcqs.q: There are 40 boys and 60 girls in a Mathematics class. What is the ratio of boys to girls in simplest form?
mcqs.why: Working: boys : girls = 40 : 60. The H.C.F of 40 and 60 is 20, so 40/20 : 60/20 = 2 : 3.

mcqs.q: Write 18 : 24 in fraction form and simplify it.
mcqs.why: Working: 18 : 24 = 18/24. Dividing numerator and denominator by 6 gives 3/4, so 18 : 24 = 3 : 4.

mcqs.q: Find the ratio of 500 g to 1 kg.
mcqs.why: Working: first use the same unit, 1 kg = 1000 g, so 500 : 1000. Dividing both terms by 500 gives 1 : 2.

mcqs.q: Naseem shared Rs. 1600 with Rabia and Fatima in the ratio 3 : 5. How much did Fatima receive?
mcqs.why: Working: total parts = 3 + 5 = 8. Fatima's share = 5/8 x 1600 = 5 x 200 = Rs. 1000. Check: 600 + 1000 = 1600.

mcqs.q: Nadia distributed Rs. 9435 in the continued ratio Nida : Rehan : Aleem = 12 : 15 : 10. How much did Rehan get?
mcqs.why: Working: sum of ratios = 12 + 15 + 10 = 37. Rehan's share = 15/37 x 9435 = 15 x 255 = Rs. 3825.

mcqs.q: Naveed completed his century in 1 hour and Sarfraz in 1 hour 30 minutes. What is the ratio of their times in simplest form?
mcqs.why: Working: convert to minutes: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 hour 30 minutes = 90 minutes, so 60 : 90. Dividing by H.C.F 30 gives 2 : 3.

lessons.title: 4.2 RATE
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Rate?

Let’s help Ali to buy bananas from the fruit shop. The first kind of bananas cost is Rs. 168 for 12 bananas. The second kind of bananas cost is Rs. 60 for 6 bananas. Which kind of bananas should Ali buy? To find the result of this problem, we have to find each of their rate for an equal number of bananas, such as one banana.

Step 1: Price of the first kind of a banana = 168/12 = Rs. 14.

Step 2: Price of the second kind of a banana = 60/6 = Rs. 10.

Step 3: Rs. 10 is less than Rs. 14, so we should suggest Ali to buy the second kind of bananas.

Final answer: Ali should buy the second kind of bananas (Rs. 10 per banana)

From the above example we conclude that “A rate is a special kind of ratio in which the two terms are in different units.” A ratio is comparison of two or more numbers or things with same units, but the rate is a special kind of ratio in which we compare two or more quantities with different units.

Example 11: Shazmeena is buying jellybeans for her sister Sofia’s birthday party. She buys a bag of 50 g of jellybeans that costs Rs. 500. Shazmeena is wondering about the cost of 1 g of jellybeans. How can she find the cost of 1 g of jellybeans?

Step 1: Cost of 50 g of jellybeans = Rs. 500; cost of 1 g of jellybeans = ?

Step 2: To find the cost of 1 g of jellybeans we need to divide as: (500 ÷ 50)/(50 ÷ 50) = 10.

Final answer: The cost of 1 g of jellybeans is Rs. 10

Worked examples — Practice-2

Nadeem pays Rs. 50 for parking his motorcycle in a shopping mall for 5 hours. Calculate the parking charges for 3 hours and 30 minutes.

Step 1: Find the rate per hour: 50 ÷ 5 = Rs. 10 per hour.

Step 2: 3 hours and 30 minutes = 3.5 hours.

Step 3: Charges = 3.5 × 10 = Rs. 35.

Final answer: Rs. 35

Worked examples — Exercise 4.2

Q1: Nimra works in an office as a secretary. Last week she worked 35 hours and earned Rs. 29,995. Calculate: (i) How much amount does Nimra earn per hour? (ii) How much amount does Nimra earn for 10 hours? (iii) How much amount does Nimra earn for 25 hours?

Step 1: Find the rate per hour: 29,995 ÷ 35 = Rs. 857 per hour.

Step 2: (ii) For 10 hours: 857 × 10 = Rs. 8,570.

Step 3: (iii) For 25 hours: 857 × 25 = Rs. 21,425.

Final answer: (i) Rs. 857 per hour (ii) Rs. 8,570 (iii) Rs. 21,425

Q2: Naureen walked 2 km and 500 m in 50 minutes. What was her rate of walking in kilometre per hour?

Step 1: Convert the distance to kilometres: 2 km and 500 m = 2.5 km.

Step 2: Convert the time to hours: 50 minutes = 50/60 hour = 5/6 hour.

Step 3: Use the formula Rate = Distance ÷ Time: rate = 2.5 ÷ (5/6) = 2.5 × 6/5 = 3 km per hour.

Final answer: 3 km per hour

Q3: Rehan drove his car at an average rate of 80 km per hour. How far did he drive in 5 hours? (Hint: Use formula; Distance = rate × time)

Step 1: Write the formula: Distance = rate × time.

Step 2: Substitute the values: Distance = 80 × 5 = 400 km.

Final answer: 400 km

Q4: Shumail takes 2 1/2 hours to paint a 15 m long wall. What is his rate of painting wall per hour?

Step 1: Write the rate as distance painted ÷ time taken: rate = 15 ÷ 2 1/2.

Step 2: 15 ÷ 5/2 = 15 × 2/5 = 6 m per hour.

Final answer: 6 m per hour

Q5: 7 kg of cooking oil costs Rs. 2415. What is the cost of 5 kg of cooking oil?

Step 1: Find the rate per kg: 2415 ÷ 7 = Rs. 345 per kg.

Step 2: Cost of 5 kg = 345 × 5 = Rs. 1725.

Final answer: Rs. 1725

Q6: Naeem has to pay Rs. 875 for 350 minutes of outgoing calls by using his mobile. Find: (i) How much amount is charged for 7 minutes of outgoing calls? (ii) The amount he has to pay if he makes 563 minutes of outgoing calls.

Step 1: Find the rate per minute: 875 ÷ 350 = Rs. 2.5 per minute.

Step 2: (i) For 7 minutes: 2.5 × 7 = Rs. 17.50.

Step 3: (ii) For 563 minutes: 2.5 × 563 = Rs. 1407.50.

Final answer: (i) Rs. 17.50 (ii) Rs. 1407.50

mcqs.q: What is a rate?
options: A special ratio in which the two terms are in different units
A ratio of two quantities with the same unit
A ratio written only as a fraction
A comparison that has no unit at all
mcqs.why: The notes state that a rate is a special kind of ratio in which the two terms are in different units, unlike an ordinary ratio which compares the same units.

mcqs.q: The first kind of bananas costs Rs. 168 for 12 bananas. What is the cost of one banana of this kind?
mcqs.why: Working: price of one banana = 168 / 12 = Rs. 14 per banana, found by dividing the total price by the number of bananas.

mcqs.q: Bananas cost Rs. 168 for 12 in one kind and Rs. 60 for 6 in another kind. Which kind should Ali buy?
options: The first kind, at Rs. 14 per banana
The second kind, at Rs. 10 per banana
Both cost the same per banana
The first kind, at Rs. 10 per banana
mcqs.why: Working: first kind = 168 / 12 = Rs. 14 per banana; second kind = 60 / 6 = Rs. 10 per banana. Rs. 10 is less than Rs. 14, so the second kind is cheaper.

mcqs.q: A bag of 50 g of jellybeans costs Rs. 500. What is the cost of 1 g of jellybeans?
mcqs.why: Working: cost of 1 g = 500 / 50 = Rs. 10, because (500 / 50) / (50 / 50) = 10 / 1 = Rs. 10 per gram.

mcqs.q: Nadeem pays Rs. 50 for parking for 5 hours. What are the parking charges for 3 hours and 30 minutes?
mcqs.why: Working: rate per hour = 50 / 5 = Rs. 10 per hour. 3 hours 30 minutes = 3.5 hours, so charges = 3.5 x 10 = Rs. 35.

mcqs.q: Nimra worked 35 hours and earned Rs. 29,995. How much does she earn per hour?
mcqs.why: Working: rate per hour = 29,995 / 35 = Rs. 857 per hour, found by dividing her total earning by the total hours worked.

mcqs.q: Nimra earns Rs. 857 per hour. How much will she earn for 25 hours?
mcqs.why: Working: earning for 25 hours = rate x time = 857 x 25 = Rs. 21,425, using the per-hour rate of Rs. 857.

mcqs.q: Naureen walked 2 km and 500 m in 50 minutes. What was her rate of walking in km per hour?
mcqs.why: Working: distance = 2.5 km, time = 50/60 = 5/6 hour. Rate = 2.5 / (5/6) = 2.5 x 6/5 = 3 km per hour.

mcqs.q: 7 kg of cooking oil costs Rs. 2415. What is the cost of 5 kg of cooking oil?
mcqs.why: Working: rate per kg = 2415 / 7 = Rs. 345 per kg. Cost of 5 kg = 345 x 5 = Rs. 1725.

mcqs.q: Naeem pays Rs. 875 for 350 minutes of outgoing calls. How much is charged for 7 minutes?
mcqs.why: Working: rate per minute = 875 / 350 = Rs. 2.5 per minute. For 7 minutes: 2.5 x 7 = Rs. 17.50.

lessons.title: 4.3 PERCENTAGE
lessons.notes_html:
What is Percentage?

We are familiar with the word percentage. We have learnt about it in our previous grade and normally hear phrases like sale, sale up to 70% off in our daily life. We apply percentages on many things, like percentage discount, percentage of obtained marks, etc. Percentage is a short form of Latin word ‘per centum’, meaning out of hundred, which means the ratio of some numbers to hundred. A symbol % is used for percent.

4.3.1 Percentage as a Fraction

Percent means the ratio of a given number to hundred. Look at the 100-square figures in the book:

  • 1 out of 100 of the squares is coloured. So, “1 per 100” or 1/100 means 1%.
  • 40 out of 100 of the squares are coloured. So, “40 per 100” or 40/100 means 40%.
  • 64 out of 100 of the squares are coloured. So, “64 per 100” or 64/100 means 64%.

4.3.2 Expressing One Quantity as Percentage of Another

It is very common to write one number as percentage of another number. For example, it is used for calculating percentage of obtained marks in a test or exam, or working out costs on a project, etc. Generally, to express one quantity as a percentage of another, write the given quantity as a fraction of the total and multiply it by 100%, or 100/100. Both the quantities are expressed in the same unit. Remember: 100% = 100/100; it means multiplying by 1 does not change the value.

Example 12: Waqar obtained 180 marks in his 1st term exams. The total marks of all his subjects are 200. Find the percentage of Waqar’s obtained marks.

Step 1: Total marks of all subjects = 200; obtained marks = 180.

Step 2: Use the formula Percentage of obtained marks = (obtained marks / total marks) × 100: = 180/200 × 100.

Step 3: 180/200 × 100 = 90%.

Final answer: Waqar obtained 90% marks in his 1st term examination

Worked examples — Practice-6

In a school, there are 13 male teachers and 20 female teachers. Calculate the percentage of (i) male teachers (ii) female teachers.

Step 1: Find the total number of teachers: 13 + 20 = 33.

Step 2: Use the formula Percentage = (given quantity / total quantity) × 100%. (i) Male teachers = 13/33 × 100% = 39.39% (approximately).

Step 3: (ii) Female teachers = 20/33 × 100% = 60.61% (approximately).

Step 4: Check: 39.39% + 60.61% = 100%. ✓

Final answer: (i) 39.39% (approximately) (ii) 60.61% (approximately)

4.3.3 Percentage of Given Quantities

Example 13: Find the percentage of the following numbers: (i) 6% of 100 (ii) 25% of 320 (iii) 42% of 1000.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction by dividing by 100: 6% = 6/100, 25% = 25/100, 42% = 42/100.

Step 2: (i) 6% of 100 = 6/100 × 100 = 6.

Step 3: (ii) 25% of 320 = 25/100 × 320 = 80.

Step 4: (iii) 42% of 1000 = 42/100 × 1000 = 420.

Final answer: (i) 6 (ii) 80 (iii) 420

Example 14: Qadeer has Rs. 2000, which is 40% of a new cycle. How much more money does he have to arrange for the cycle?

Step 1: 40% of total price of cycle = 2000.

Step 2: Use the formula Total quantity = Given quantity ÷ percentage: Total price of cycle = 2000 ÷ 40%.

Step 3: 2000 ÷ 40/100 = 2000 × 100/40 = 5000. So, the total price of cycle is Rs. 5000.

Step 4: More required money = 5000 − 2000 = 3000.

Final answer: Qadeer needs Rs. 3000 more to buy a new cycle

Remember: To calculate the total quantity always use the formula Total quantity = Given quantity ÷ percentage.

Worked examples — Practice-3

Practice-3 (i): Find the value of 15% of 150.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction: 15% = 15/100.

Step 2: 15% of 150 = 15/100 × 150 = 22.5.

Final answer: 22.5

Practice-3 (ii): Find the value of 1000% of Rs. 13.50.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction: 1000% = 1000/100 = 10.

Step 2: 1000% of 13.50 = 10 × 13.50 = Rs. 135.

Final answer: Rs. 135

4.3.4 Comparison of two Quantities by Percentage

Alina says: in my school 550 out of 600 students passed the final exams and got promoted to next grades. Ali says: in my school 380 out of 400 students passed the final exams and got promoted to next grade. Since 550 > 380, does this mean that Alina’s school result is better than Ali’s school result? To handle this type of situation, we find the percentage result of both schools and compare their results.

  • Alina’s school result: Percentage result = 550/600 × 100% = 91.67%.
  • Ali’s school result: Percentage result = 380/400 × 100% = 95%.

As the percentage result of Ali’s school is greater than Alina’s school result, Ali’s school performed better.

Example 15: There are two bags, A and B. Bag A contains 80 white marbles out of 350 total marbles. Bag B contains 65 white marbles out of 200 total marbles. Which bag contains higher percentage of white marbles?

Step 1: Bag A: white marbles percentage = 80/350 × 100% = 22.86%.

Step 2: Bag B: white marbles percentage = 65/200 × 100% = 32.5%.

Step 3: Compare: 32.5% > 22.86%.

Final answer: Bag B contains higher percentage of white marbles

Worked examples — Practice-4

In an election, candidate A got 14570 votes out of 20,000 total votes. Candidate B got 13495 votes out of 15000 total votes. Which candidate got more votes? Also, calculate the percentage votes of each candidate.

Step 1: Compare the raw votes: 14570 > 13495, so candidate A got more votes in number.

Step 2: Use the formula Percentage = (votes obtained / total votes) × 100%. Candidate A = 14570/20000 × 100% = 72.85%.

Step 3: Candidate B = 13495/15000 × 100% = 89.97% (approximately).

Step 4: Compare the percentages: 89.97% > 72.85%, so candidate B got the higher percentage of votes.

Final answer: Candidate A got more votes in number (14570); Candidate A = 72.85%, Candidate B = 89.97% (approximately), so Candidate B has the higher percentage

4.3.5 Increasing or Decreasing of a Quantity by a Given Percentage

In our routine life, we observe changes happen everyday. We calculate percentage increase/decrease and express the increase/decrease amount as percentage.

Example 16: A shopkeeper increases the price of an article by 10% from its original price. If the original price of the article is Rs. 5650, what will be the new price of the article?

Step 1: An increase of 10% means for every Rs. 100 of the original price, there is an increase of Rs. 10. So, each Rs. 100 in the original price becomes Rs. 110 in the new price. Therefore, new price : original price = 110 : 100.

Step 2: The fraction form is New price / Original price = 110/100, so New price = 110/100 × original price.

Step 3: New price = 110/100 × 5650 = Rs. 6215.

Step 4: Increase in price = new price − original price = Rs. 6215 − Rs. 5650 = Rs. 565.

Final answer: New price Rs. 6215; the shopkeeper has increased Rs. 565 in the original price

Example 17: The original price of petrol is Rs. 161 per litre. If the government decreases its price by 12%, then what will be the new price? Also, calculate the decreased amount.

Step 1: A decrease of 12% means for every Rs. 100 of the original price, there is a decrease of Rs. 12, i.e. each Rs. 100 in the original price becomes Rs. 88 in the new price. So, new price : original price = 88 : 100.

Step 2: The fraction form is New price / Original price = 88/100, so New price = 88/100 × original price.

Step 3: New price = 88/100 × 161 = Rs. 141.68.

Step 4: Decrease in price = original price − new price = 161 − 141.68 = Rs. 19.32.

Final answer: New price Rs. 141.68 per litre; decreased amount Rs. 19.32

In general we use the formulas: (i) New value = final percentage × original value. (ii) Increase/decrease = percentage increase/decrease × original value.

Example 18: The price of a calculator is decreased from Rs. 2000 to Rs. 1340, but the price of a school bag is raised from Rs. 1799 to Rs. 2295. Find the percentage increase and percentage decrease of both prices.

Step 1: Calculator: original price = Rs. 2000, new price = Rs. 1340. Decreased amount = 2000 − 1340 = Rs. 660.

Step 2: Use the formula Percentage decrease = (Decrease / Original price) × 100%: = 660/2000 × 100% = 33%. Hence, the price of calculator is decreased by 33%.

Step 3: School bag: original price = Rs. 1799, new price = Rs. 2295. Increased amount = 2295 − 1799 = Rs. 496.

Step 4: Use the formula Percentage increase = (Increase / Original price) × 100%: = 496/1799 × 100% = 27.6%. Hence, the price of school bag is increased by 27.6%.

Final answer: Calculator decreased by 33%; School bag increased by 27.6%

Worked examples — Practice-5

Practice-5 (i): Increase 65 by 130%, what is the result?

Step 1: Find the increase: 130% of 65 = 130/100 × 65 = 84.5.

Step 2: New value = original value + increase = 65 + 84.5 = 149.5.

Final answer: 149.5

Practice-5 (ii): Decrease 125 by 65%, what is the result?

Step 1: Find the decrease: 65% of 125 = 65/100 × 125 = 81.25.

Step 2: New value = original value − decrease = 125 − 81.25 = 43.75.

Final answer: 43.75

Practice-5 (iii): In 2019, Naeem was given 10% increment in his basic salary of Rs. 25500. Find his new salary after increment.

Step 1: Find the increment: 10% of 25500 = 10/100 × 25500 = Rs. 2550.

Step 2: New salary = 25500 + 2550 = Rs. 28050.

Final answer: Rs. 28050

Practice-5 (iv): In 2020, due to pandemic of Covid-19 Nadia suffered a pay cut of 20% in her basic pay of Rs. 30,000. Find her new salary after cut off.

Step 1: Find the cut: 20% of 30,000 = 20/100 × 30,000 = Rs. 6,000.

Step 2: New salary = 30,000 − 6,000 = Rs. 24,000.

Final answer: Rs. 24,000

Worked examples — Exercise 4.3

Q1: Write the percentage of the coloured part of each figure: (i) a 100-square grid with 33 squares coloured (10 + 10 + 7 + 6 by rows) (ii) a 100-square grid with 29 squares coloured (10 + 3 + 3 + 10 + 2 + 1) (iii) a circle with half of it coloured.

Step 1: Percent means the ratio of a given number to hundred, so count the coloured parts out of 100.

Step 2: (i) Coloured squares = 10 + 10 + 7 + 6 = 33, so the coloured part is 33/100 = 33%.

Step 3: (ii) Coloured squares = 10 + 3 + 3 + 10 + 2 + 1 = 29, so the coloured part is 29/100 = 29%.

Step 4: (iii) Half of the circle is coloured: 1/2 = 50/100 = 50%.

Final answer: (i) 33% (ii) 29% (iii) 50%

Q2: Write the following percentages into the simplified form of fraction: (i) 25% (ii) 20% (iii) 84% (iv) 34% (v) 93%.

Step 1: Write each percentage as a fraction with denominator 100: (i) 25/100 (ii) 20/100 (iii) 84/100 (iv) 34/100 (v) 93/100.

Step 2: Simplify each fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by their H.C.F: (i) 25/100 = 1/4 (ii) 20/100 = 1/5 (iii) 84/100 = 21/25 (iv) 34/100 = 17/50 (v) 93/100 cannot be simplified.

Final answer: (i) 1/4 (ii) 1/5 (iii) 21/25 (iv) 17/50 (v) 93/100

Q3(i): Solve: 8% of 100.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction: 8% = 8/100.

Step 2: 8% of 100 = 8/100 × 100 = 8.

Final answer: 8

Q3(ii): Solve: 15% of 60 litres.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction: 15% = 15/100.

Step 2: 15% of 60 = 15/100 × 60 = 9 litres.

Final answer: 9 litres

Q3(iii): Solve: 35% of 160.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction: 35% = 35/100.

Step 2: 35% of 160 = 35/100 × 160 = 56.

Final answer: 56

Q3(iv): Solve: 80% of 900.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction: 80% = 80/100.

Step 2: 80% of 900 = 80/100 × 900 = 720.

Final answer: 720

Q3(v): Solve: 9 1/4% of 1000.

Step 1: Change the mixed percentage into a decimal percentage: 9 1/4% = 9.25% = 9.25/100.

Step 2: 9 1/4% of 1000 = 9.25/100 × 1000 = 92.5.

Final answer: 92.5

Q3(vi): Solve: 3 3/8% of 80.

Step 1: Change the mixed percentage into a decimal percentage: 3 3/8% = 3.375% = 3.375/100.

Step 2: 3 3/8% of 80 = 3.375/100 × 80 = 2.7.

Final answer: 2.7

Q3(vii): Solve: 9.8% of 80.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction: 9.8% = 9.8/100.

Step 2: 9.8% of 80 = 9.8/100 × 80 = 7.84.

Final answer: 7.84

Q3(viii): Solve: 8.9% of 900.

Step 1: Change the percentage into a fraction: 8.9% = 8.9/100.

Step 2: 8.9% of 900 = 8.9/100 × 900 = 80.1.

Final answer: 80.1

Q4: Nimra obtained 125 marks out of 250. Calculate the percentage of obtained marks of Nimra.

Step 1: Use the formula Percentage of obtained marks = (obtained marks / total marks) × 100.

Step 2: Percentage = 125/250 × 100 = 50%.

Final answer: 50%

Q5: There are 400 students in a school. 30% of them are left handed. How many students are right handed?

Step 1: Find the left handed students: 30% of 400 = 30/100 × 400 = 120 students.

Step 2: Right handed students = total students − left handed students = 400 − 120 = 280 students.

Final answer: 280 students

Q6: 65% of the students come from Govt. High School Model Town. If there are 1500 students in the school, then find how many students are not from Model Town.

Step 1: Find the students from Model Town: 65% of 1500 = 65/100 × 1500 = 975 students.

Step 2: Students not from Model Town = 1500 − 975 = 525 students.

Final answer: 525 students

Q7: Your Mathematics class is of 40 minutes duration. Your teacher spends 15 minutes to check copy work and the remaining time to complete a mathematical activity. Find the percentage of: (i) time spent for copy work (ii) time spent for mathematical activity.

Step 1: Find the time for the mathematical activity: 40 − 15 = 25 minutes.

Step 2: Use the formula Percentage = (given quantity / total quantity) × 100%. (i) Copy work = 15/40 × 100% = 37.5%.

Step 3: (ii) Mathematical activity = 25/40 × 100% = 62.5%.

Step 4: Check: 37.5% + 62.5% = 100%. ✓

Final answer: (i) 37.5% (ii) 62.5%

Q8: Anee spends 80% of the total earning at the golf course last summer. If she spends Rs. 35,000, then find her total earning at golf course.

Step 1: 80% of the total earning = Rs. 35,000.

Step 2: Use the formula Total quantity = Given quantity ÷ percentage: Total earning = 35,000 ÷ 80%.

Step 3: 35,000 ÷ 80/100 = 35,000 × 100/80 = Rs. 43,750.

Final answer: Rs. 43,750

Q9: The 20% of a number is 120. Find the number.

Step 1: 20% of the number = 120.

Step 2: Use the formula Total quantity = Given quantity ÷ percentage: Number = 120 ÷ 20%.

Step 3: 120 ÷ 20/100 = 120 × 100/20 = 600.

Final answer: 600

Q10: The 70% of a tree is 3.8 m. Find the total height of the tree.

Step 1: 70% of the total height = 3.8 m.

Step 2: Use the formula Total quantity = Given quantity ÷ percentage: Total height = 3.8 ÷ 70%.

Step 3: 3.8 ÷ 70/100 = 3.8 × 100/70 = 5.43 m (approximately).

Final answer: 5.43 m (approximately)

Q11: 20% of the students of a school were absent on a certain day. If there were 1200 students present in the school on that day, then find the total number of students.

Step 1: Find the percentage of present students: 100% − 20% = 80%. So 80% of the total students = 1200.

Step 2: Use the formula Total quantity = Given quantity ÷ percentage: Total students = 1200 ÷ 80%.

Step 3: 1200 ÷ 80/100 = 1200 × 100/80 = 1500.

Final answer: 1500 students

Q12: Nadia used 6 kg of Banaspati Ghee out of 8 kg Banaspati Ghee in the month of March. She used 7 kg of Banaspati Ghee out of 10 kg Banaspati Ghee in the month of April. In which month did she use more Ghee than the other month?

Step 1: Find the percentage used in March: 6/8 × 100% = 75%.

Step 2: Find the percentage used in April: 7/10 × 100% = 70%.

Step 3: Compare: 75% > 70%.

Final answer: She used more Ghee (percentage-wise) in March

Q13: In the month of Ramadan, Saleem donated Rs. 4500 to charity from his total salary of Rs. 45000. Aleem donated Rs. 6000 to charity from his salary of Rs. 55000. Who has donated the higher percentage of his monthly salary?

Step 1: Use the formula Percentage = (given quantity / total quantity) × 100%. Saleem = 4500/45000 × 100% = 10%.

Step 2: Aleem = 6000/55000 × 100% = 10.91% (approximately).

Step 3: Compare: 10.91% > 10%.

Final answer: Aleem donated the higher percentage (10.91% approximately, against Saleem’s 10%)

Q14: Increase 17 by 85%, what is the result?

Step 1: Find the increase: 85% of 17 = 85/100 × 17 = 14.45.

Step 2: New value = original value + increase = 17 + 14.45 = 31.45.

Final answer: 31.45

Q15: Decrease 30 by 70%, what is the result?

Step 1: Find the decrease: 70% of 30 = 70/100 × 30 = 21.

Step 2: New value = original value − decrease = 30 − 21 = 9.

Final answer: 9

Q16: In the month of September Salma got 15% increase in her monthly salary. If Salma’s monthly salary is Rs. 45000, then what is her new salary?

Step 1: Find the increase: 15% of 45000 = 15/100 × 45000 = Rs. 6750.

Step 2: New salary = 45000 + 6750 = Rs. 51750.

Final answer: Rs. 51750

Q17: After 12% of a bill has been deducted, Rs. 6536 remains to be paid. How much was the original bill?

Step 1: Find the percentage that remains: 100% − 12% = 88%. So 88% of the original bill = Rs. 6536.

Step 2: Use the formula Total quantity = Given quantity ÷ percentage: Original bill = 6536 ÷ 88%.

Step 3: 6536 ÷ 88/100 = 6536 × 100/88 = Rs. 7427.27 (approximately).

Final answer: Rs. 7427.27 (approximately)

Q18: The cost of a bicycle is raised from Rs. 8500 to Rs. 10,000. What is the percentage increase in the price of bicycle?

Step 1: Find the increase: 10,000 − 8500 = Rs. 1500.

Step 2: Use the formula Percentage increase = (Increase / Original price) × 100%: = 1500/8500 × 100%.

Step 3: 1500/8500 × 100% = 17.65% (approximately).

Final answer: 17.65% (approximately)

mcqs.q: If 64 out of 100 squares are coloured, what percentage is coloured?
mcqs.why: Percent means out of hundred, so 64 out of 100 is written as 64/100, which means 64% of the squares are coloured.

mcqs.q: Write 84% as a fraction in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: Working: 84% = 84/100. Dividing numerator and denominator by their H.C.F 4 gives 84/4 / 100/4 = 21/25.

mcqs.q: Waqar obtained 180 marks out of 200. What is the percentage of his obtained marks?
mcqs.why: Working: percentage = (obtained / total) x 100 = 180/200 x 100 = 0.9 x 100 = 90%, so Waqar obtained 90% marks.

mcqs.q: Find 25% of 320.
Qadeer has Rs. 2000, which is 40% of the price of a new cycle. How much more money does he need?
mcqs.why: Working: total price = 2000 / 40% = 2000 x 100/40 = Rs. 5000. More money needed = 5000 - 2000 = Rs. 3000.

mcqs.q: Bag A has 80 white marbles out of 350, and Bag B has 65 white marbles out of 200. Which bag has the higher percentage of white marbles?
mcqs.why: Working: Bag A = 80/350 x 100% = 22.86%. Bag B = 65/200 x 100% = 32.5%. Since 32.5% is greater than 22.86%, Bag B is higher.

mcqs.q: There are 400 students in a school and 30% are left handed. How many students are right handed?
mcqs.why: Working: left handed = 30% of 400 = 30/100 x 400 = 120 students. Right handed = 400 - 120 = 280 students.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper increases the price of an article from Rs. 5650 by 10%. What is the new price?
mcqs.why: Working: new price = 110/100 x 5650 = Rs. 6215. The increase itself is 6215 - 5650 = Rs. 565, which is 10% of 5650.

mcqs.q: The price of petrol is Rs. 161 per litre. If it is decreased by 12%, what is the new price?
mcqs.why: Working: a 12% decrease means the new price is 88% of the old price, so new price = 88/100 x 161 = Rs. 141.68 per litre.

mcqs.q: The price of a calculator is decreased from Rs. 2000 to Rs. 1340. What is the percentage decrease?
mcqs.why: Working: decrease = 2000 - 1340 = Rs. 660. Percentage decrease = 660/2000 x 100% = 33%, so the price decreased by 33%.

lessons.title: 4.4 TIME
lessons.notes_html:
12-Hours Clock and 24-Hours Clock

Let’s observe two clocks: the 24-hours clock and the 12-hours clock. As we know, there are 24 hours in a day. To record time of the day we simply use the 12 hours or 24 hours clock.

On the 12-hours number line: Midnight 12:00 AM, 2:00 AM, 4:00 AM, 6:00 AM, 8:00 AM, 10:00 AM, Noon (mid day) 12:00 PM, 2:00 PM, 4:00 PM, 6:00 PM, 8:00 PM, 10:00 PM, Midnight 12:00 AM. So 12 hours (before noon) + 12 hours (after noon) = 24 hours or 1 day.

On the 24-hours number line: Midnight 00, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, Noon (mid day) 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, Midnight 24. So 24 hours = 1 day.

  • a.m. stands for “ante meridiem”, which means before mid day.
  • p.m. stands for “post meridiem”, which means “after mid day”.

Example 19: Waqas leaves Lahore at 22:30 on Sunday and arrives Pirmahal 2 1/2 hours later. At what time did Waqas reach Pirmahal?

Step 1: Since 2 1/2 hours = 2 hours, 30 minutes.

Step 2: Add the travelling time to the starting time on the number line: 22:30 + 2 hours 30 minutes passes 00:00 (midnight) and reaches 01:00.

Final answer: Waqas arrives Pirmahal at 01:00, or 01:00 a.m., on Monday

Worked examples — Practice-6

Ajmal started playing cricket at 14:45 and ends at 18:00. How much time did he spend while playing cricket?

Step 1: Both times are in the 24-hours clock. Subtract the start time from the end time: 18:00 − 14:45.

Step 2: From 14:45 to 15:00 is 15 minutes, and from 15:00 to 18:00 is 3 hours.

Step 3: Total time = 3 hours + 15 minutes = 3 hours 15 minutes.

Final answer: 3 hours 15 minutes

Worked examples — Exercise 4.4

Q1: Convert the following 12-hours clock time into 24-hours clock time: (i) 7:45 p.m. (ii) 9:31 a.m. (iii) 8:35 p.m.

Step 1: For a.m. times (before noon), the hours stay the same. For p.m. times (after noon), add 12 to the hours.

Step 2: (i) 7:45 p.m. = 7 + 12 = 19:45. (ii) 9:31 a.m. = 09:31. (iii) 8:35 p.m. = 8 + 12 = 20:35.

Final answer: (i) 19:45 (ii) 09:31 (iii) 20:35

Q2: Convert the following 24-hours clock time into 12-hours clock time: (i) 15:48 (ii) 23:15 (iii) 19:43.

Step 1: For times after 12:00 (noon), subtract 12 from the hours and write p.m. Times before noon are written with a.m.

Step 2: (i) 15:48 = 15 − 12 = 3:48 p.m. (ii) 23:15 = 23 − 12 = 11:15 p.m. (iii) 19:43 = 19 − 12 = 7:43 p.m.

Final answer: (i) 3:48 p.m. (ii) 11:15 p.m. (iii) 7:43 p.m.

Q3: A bus leaves for Peshawar at 4:30 p.m. It takes 6 hours to reach there. What time will it reach in Peshawar?

Step 1: Add the travelling time to the leaving time: 4:30 p.m. + 6 hours.

Step 2: 4:30 + 6 hours = 10:30, and it is still before midnight, so the time is p.m.

Final answer: 10:30 p.m.

Q4: Nadia sleeps for 6 hours 30 minutes in a day. Today if she sleeps at 22:15, then at what time will she wake up?

Step 1: Add the sleeping time to the sleeping start time: 22:15 + 6 hours 30 minutes.

Step 2: 22:15 + 6 hours = 04:15 (next day, after passing midnight 24:00), then + 30 minutes = 04:45.

Final answer: 04:45 (4:45 a.m. next day)

Q5: The arrival time of Allama Iqbal Express at Lahore junction is 11:40 a.m. and its departure time is 12:10 p.m. How much time did Allama Iqbal Express stay at Lahore junction?

Step 1: Subtract the arrival time from the departure time: 12:10 p.m. − 11:40 a.m.

Step 2: From 11:40 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 20 minutes, and from 12:00 noon to 12:10 p.m. is 10 minutes.

Step 3: Total stay = 20 + 10 = 30 minutes.

Final answer: 30 minutes

mcqs.q: What does a.m. stand for and mean?
options: Ante meridiem, meaning before mid day
mcqs.why: The notes state that a.m. stands for ante meridiem, which means before mid day, covering the 12 hours from midnight to noon.

mcqs.q: What does p.m. mean?
options: Post meridiem, meaning after mid day
mcqs.why: The notes state that p.m. stands for post meridiem, which means after mid day, covering the 12 hours from noon to midnight.

mcqs.q: Convert 7:45 p.m. into 24-hours clock time.
mcqs.why: Working: for a p.m. time after noon, add 12 to the hours: 7 + 12 = 19, so 7:45 p.m. = 19:45 in the 24-hours clock.

mcqs.q: Convert 15:48 into 12-hours clock time.
mcqs.why: Working: 15:48 is after noon, so subtract 12 from the hours: 15 - 12 = 3, and write p.m., giving 3:48 p.m.

mcqs.q: Convert 23:15 into 12-hours clock time.
mcqs.why: Working: 23:15 is after noon, so subtract 12 from the hours: 23 - 12 = 11, and write p.m., giving 11:15 p.m.

mcqs.q: Waqas leaves Lahore at 22:30 on Sunday and travels for 2 and a half hours. At what time does he reach Pirmahal?
mcqs.why: Working: 22:30 + 2 hours 30 minutes passes midnight 00:00 and reaches 01:00, so he arrives at 01:00 a.m. on Monday.

mcqs.q: Ajmal started playing cricket at 14:45 and ended at 18:00. How long did he play?
mcqs.why: Working: from 14:45 to 15:00 is 15 minutes, and from 15:00 to 18:00 is 3 hours, so total time = 3 hours + 15 minutes = 3 hours 15 minutes.

mcqs.q: Nadia sleeps at 22:15 and sleeps for 6 hours 30 minutes. At what time will she wake up?
mcqs.why: Working: 22:15 + 6 hours = 04:15 next day after passing midnight, then + 30 minutes = 04:45, so she wakes at 04:45.

mcqs.q: A train arrives at 11:40 a.m. and departs at 12:10 p.m. How long did it stay at the station?
mcqs.why: Working: from 11:40 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 20 minutes, and from noon to 12:10 p.m. is 10 minutes, so total stay = 20 + 10 = 30 minutes.

mcqs.q: Convert 8:35 p.m. into 24-hours clock time.
mcqs.why: Working: for a p.m. time, add 12 to the hours: 8 + 12 = 20, so 8:35 p.m. = 20:35 in the 24-hours clock.

lessons.title: 4.5 RELATION BETWEEN DISTANCE, TIME AND SPEED
lessons.notes_html:
Relation Between Distance, Time and Speed

We plan to travel; we always choose an appropriate means which takes less time to cover more distance. Time and distance are related to each other with speed. For example, Zurain is travelling from Lahore to Bahawalpur. The distance covered by Zurain’s car from Lahore to Bahawalpur at various intervals of time is shown below:

Time1h2h3h4h5h
Distance covered86km172km258km344km430km

As more time taken covers more distance. Now look at the following table, which shows the time taken by Zurain’s car to travel from Lahore to Bahawalpur at various speeds:

Speed of car43km/h86km/h129km/h
Time taken10h5h3h

As more the speed of car, it takes less time to cover the distance from Lahore to Bahawalpur. When an object moves in a straight line at a speed, we can calculate its speed if we know how far it travels and how long it takes. This equation shows the relation between speed, distance travelled and time taken, i.e. Speed = Distance travelled / Time taken. The unit of speed is km/h (it is a common unit).

Example 20: Nadeem covers a distance of 150 km on his motorcycle in 3 hours. Calculate the speed of his motorcycle.

Step 1: Distance covered by Nadeem’s motorcycle = 150 km; time taken = 3 hours; speed of motorcycle = ?

Step 2: Use the formula Speed = Distance travelled / Time taken: Speed = 150 km / 3 h = 50 km/h.

Final answer: The speed of Nadeem’s motorcycle is 50 km/h

4.5.1 Conversion of Unit of Speed (Kilometre per Hour, Metre per Second and Vice Versa)

The most common unit of speed is kilometre/hour or miles per hour. These are the units that the speedometer of your vehicle will show. There are also a few other units of speed, such as metre per second and kilometre per second, etc.

Remember: 1 km = 1000 m; 1 m = 100 cm; 1 hour = 60 minutes; 1 minute = 60 seconds; 1 hour = 3600 seconds.

To convert kilometre per hour to metre per second: Kilometre/Hour = 1 km / 1 hour = (1 × 1000 m) / (1 × (60 × 60) sec) = 1000 m / 3600 sec = 5/18 m/sec. So we can convert km/h into m/sec by multiplying by 5/18.

Example 21: Convert 100 km/h into m/sec.

Step 1: Use the rule: multiply by 5/18, because 1 km/h = 5/18 m/sec.

Step 2: 100 km/h = 100 × 5/18 m/sec = 27.78 m/sec.

Final answer: 27.78 m/sec

Example 22: The speed of a car is 150 km/hour. Find the speed of car in metre per second.

Step 1: The speed of car = 150 km/hour, and 1 km/h = 5/18 m/sec.

Step 2: 150 × 5/18 m/sec = 41.7 m/sec.

Final answer: 41.7 m/sec

To convert metre per second to kilometre per hour: Metre/Second = 1 m / 1 sec = (1/1000 km) / (1/(60 × 60) h) = 18/5 km/h. So we can convert m/sec into km/h just by multiplying by 18/5.

Example 23: Saba’s car covers a distance of 2000 m in 5 minutes. Calculate the speed of her car in km/h.

Step 1: Distance covered by Saba’s car = 2000 m; time taken to cover the distance of 2000 m = 5 minutes; speed of car = ?

Step 2: Use the formula Speed = Distance travelled / Time taken: Speed = 2000 m / 5 minutes = 2000 m / (5 × 60 sec) = 2000 m / 300 sec = 6.7 m/sec.

Step 3: Convert m/sec into km/h by multiplying by 18/5, because 1 m/sec = 18/5 km/h: 6.7 × 18/5 km/h = 24.12 km/h.

Final answer: The speed of Saba’s car is 24.12 km/h

Worked examples — Practice-7

Express 45 m/s in km/h.

Step 1: To convert m/sec into km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Step 2: 45 × 18/5 = 162 km/h.

Final answer: 162 km/h

Express 150 km/h in m/s.

Step 1: To convert km/h into m/sec, multiply by 5/18.

Step 2: 150 × 5/18 = 41.67 m/sec (approximately; the book’s Example 22 gives 41.7 m/sec).

Final answer: 41.7 m/sec (approximately)

Worked examples — Exercise 4.5

Q1: Convert the following into m/sec: (i) 14 km/h (ii) 40 1/2 km/h (iii) 250 km/h.

Step 1: To convert km/h into m/sec, multiply by 5/18.

Step 2: (i) 14 × 5/18 = 3.89 m/sec (approximately).

Step 3: (ii) 40 1/2 × 5/18 = 40.5 × 5/18 = 11.25 m/sec.

Step 4: (iii) 250 × 5/18 = 69.44 m/sec (approximately).

Final answer: (i) 3.89 m/sec (approximately) (ii) 11.25 m/sec (iii) 69.44 m/sec (approximately)

Q2: Convert the following into km/h: (i) 25 m/sec (ii) 130 m/sec (iii) 340 1/2 m/sec.

Step 1: To convert m/sec into km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Step 2: (i) 25 × 18/5 = 90 km/h.

Step 3: (ii) 130 × 18/5 = 468 km/h.

Step 4: (iii) 340 1/2 × 18/5 = 340.5 × 18/5 = 1225.8 km/h.

Final answer: (i) 90 km/h (ii) 468 km/h (iii) 1225.8 km/h

Q3: A car travels a distance of 749 km in 7 hours. What was the speed of car?

Step 1: Use the formula Speed = Distance travelled / Time taken.

Step 2: Speed = 749 ÷ 7 = 107 km/h.

Final answer: 107 km/h

Q4: Neelam cycles for 4 hours at a speed of 40 km/h. How much distance did she cover?

Step 1: Use the formula Distance = Speed × Time.

Step 2: Distance = 40 × 4 = 160 km.

Final answer: 160 km

Q5: A bus travels from one station to the other station, a distance of 672 km in 7 hours. The bus is only allowed to travel at 95 km/h. Did the bus break the speed limit?

Step 1: Use the formula Speed = Distance travelled / Time taken: Speed = 672 ÷ 7 = 96 km/h.

Step 2: Compare with the allowed speed: 96 km/h > 95 km/h.

Final answer: Yes, the bus broke the speed limit (96 km/h is more than 95 km/h)

Q6: Shumaila is driving across the country. For the first 4 hours, she travels at 80 km/h. For the next 3 hours, she travels 90 km/h. Assuming that she has not stopped, what is her average travelling speed in km/h?

Step 1: Find the distance of the first part: Distance = Speed × Time = 80 × 4 = 320 km.

Step 2: Find the distance of the second part: 90 × 3 = 270 km.

Step 3: Total distance = 320 + 270 = 590 km. Total time = 4 + 3 = 7 hours.

Step 4: Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time = 590 ÷ 7 = 84.29 km/h (approximately).

Final answer: 84.29 km/h (approximately)

Summary of the Sub-Domain

  • The ratio is a comparison between two numbers or things of same kinds.
  • Ratio can be written in three forms: (i) Word form (ii) Ratio form (iii) Fraction form.
  • Ratio is unit less, or it has no unit.
  • The first term in ratio is called antecedent, while the second term is called consequent.
  • A rate is a special kind of ratio, in which the two terms are in different units.
  • Any ratio having second term 100 is called percentage.
  • We use the symbol “%” instead of writing the word percentage.
  • Any fraction can be written as percentage by multiplying 100/100 or 100%.
  • For increasing or decreasing of a quantity in a given percentage, generally we use the formulae: (i) New price = Final percentage × original price (ii) Increase/decrease = percentage increase/decrease × original value.

mcqs.q: Which formula gives the speed of a moving object?
mcqs.why: The notes give the relation Speed = Distance travelled / Time taken, and the common unit of speed is km/h.

mcqs.q: Nadeem covers 150 km on his motorcycle in 3 hours. What is the speed of his motorcycle?
mcqs.why: Working: Speed = Distance / Time = 150 km / 3 h = 50 km/h, so the motorcycle travels at 50 km/h.

mcqs.q: Convert 100 km/h into metres per second.
mcqs.why: Working: to convert km/h to m/sec multiply by 5/18, so 100 x 5/18 = 500/18 = 27.78 m/sec.

mcqs.q: Express 45 m/s in km/h.
mcqs.why: Working: to convert m/sec to km/h multiply by 18/5, so 45 x 18/5 = 9 x 18 = 162 km/h.

mcqs.q: A car travels 749 km in 7 hours. What was the speed of the car?
mcqs.why: Working: Speed = Distance / Time = 749 / 7 = 107 km/h, so the car travelled at 107 km/h.

mcqs.q: Neelam cycles for 4 hours at a speed of 40 km/h. How much distance did she cover?
mcqs.why: Working: Distance = Speed x Time = 40 x 4 = 160 km, so Neelam covered a distance of 160 km.

mcqs.q: A bus travels 672 km in 7 hours where the limit is 95 km/h. Did the bus break the speed limit?
options: Yes, its speed was 96 km/h, above the limit
No, its speed was 95 km/h exactly
mcqs.why: Working: Speed = 672 / 7 = 96 km/h. Since 96 km/h is more than the allowed 95 km/h, the bus broke the speed limit.

mcqs.q: Shumaila travels 4 hours at 80 km/h and then 3 hours at 90 km/h without stopping. What is her average speed?
mcqs.why: Working: distances are 80 x 4 = 320 km and 90 x 3 = 270 km. Total = 590 km in 7 hours, so average speed = 590 / 7 = 84.29 km/h approximately.

mcqs.q: The speed of a car is 150 km/h. What is this speed in metres per second?
mcqs.why: Working: to convert km/h to m/sec multiply by 5/18, so 150 x 5/18 = 750/18 = 41.7 m/sec.

mcqs.q: In Zurain's table, the car takes 10 hours at 43 km/h and 5 hours at 86 km/h for the same journey. What does this show?
options: More speed means less time to cover the same distance
mcqs.why: When the speed doubled from 43 km/h to 86 km/h, the time halved from 10 hours to 5 hours, showing that greater speed takes less time for the same distance.

chapters.title: Unit 5: Numbers and Operations — Sub-Domain 5: Sets

lessons.title: Introduction
lessons.notes_html:
What is a set?

In our daily life we often use some words which mean a collection or a grouping. For example: a pile of books, a bunch of keys, the school uniform a student wears, and the Pakistan cricket team.

In Mathematics we use the word set to describe any collection of objects: A set is a collection of well-defined and distinct objects.

Well-defined means clearly described. There should be no uncertainty about which object belongs to the set and which does not. Distinct means no two objects of a set are identical.

Examples that are NOT sets

(i) All good teachers in Punjab who participated in the contest. (ii) All good storybooks in the library.

Step 1: Look at the word good in both statements.

Step 2: The word good is not well-defined, because a teacher may be good in the view of one person but may not be good for another. Similarly, a storybook may be good in the view of one person but may not be good for others.

Final answer: These are not sets, because good is not well-defined.

How the same examples become sets

(iii) All teachers of Mathematics in Punjab who participated in the contest. Here the word Mathematics makes the statement true for a set.

(iv) All English storybooks in the library. Here the word English makes the statement true for a set.

History

George Cantor (1854–1981 as printed in the book) was a Mathematician of the 19th century. He was the first person who gave the concept of set theory, which became the fundamental theory in Mathematics.

In this unit we will learn in detail about sets, their notations and different types.

mcqs.q: In Mathematics, what is a set?
options: Any collection of objects, even if it is unclear
A collection of well-defined and distinct objects
A group in which objects may be repeated
mcqs.why: The notes define a set as a collection of well-defined and distinct objects, so both conditions must hold together.

mcqs.q: What does 'well-defined' mean for a set?
options: The objects are written in capital letters
It is clearly described, with no uncertainty about which object belongs and which does not
mcqs.why: Well-defined means clearly described: there should be no uncertainty about which object belongs to the set and which does not.

mcqs.q: What does 'distinct' mean for the objects of a set?
options: No two objects of the set are identical
mcqs.why: Distinct means no two objects of a set are identical, so the same object is not counted as two separate members.

mcqs.q: Why is 'All good teachers in Punjab who participated in the contest' NOT a set?
options: Because the contest had no participants
Because 'good' is not well-defined — a teacher may be good for one person but not for another
mcqs.why: The word 'good' depends on personal opinion, so membership is uncertain. A set must be well-defined, therefore this is not a set.

mcqs.q: Why is 'All good storybooks in the library' NOT a set?
options: Because 'good' is not well-defined — a book may seem good to one person but not to others
Because a library has no storybooks
mcqs.why: Just like 'good teachers', the word 'good' here is a matter of opinion, so we cannot decide exactly which books belong.

mcqs.q: Which of the following IS a set, according to the notes?
options: All good teachers in Punjab who participated in the contest
All teachers of Mathematics in Punjab who participated in the contest
All good storybooks in the library
All clever pupils in the school
mcqs.why: Replacing 'good' with 'Mathematics' makes membership exact — a teacher either teaches Mathematics or does not — so it is well-defined.

mcqs.q: Which of the following IS a set, according to the notes?
options: All good storybooks in the library
All interesting storybooks in the library
All English storybooks in the library
All favourite storybooks in the library
mcqs.why: The word 'English' gives an exact test — a book is either in English or it is not — so the collection is well-defined and is a set.

mcqs.q: Which daily-life phrase in the notes shows the idea of a collection or grouping?
mcqs.why: The notes give a pile of books, a bunch of keys, a school uniform and the Pakistan cricket team as everyday words for a collection.

mcqs.q: Who was the first person to give the concept of set theory?
mcqs.why: The notes name George Cantor, a mathematician of the 19th century, as the first person who gave the concept of set theory.

mcqs.q: According to the notes, what did set theory become in Mathematics?
options: A chapter that was later removed
